okuma-pidgin-ve-kreol.t: Tok Pisin, whose name derives from the English words 'talk pidgin', is today one of the official languages of Papua New Guinea and is understood by much of the country's population. Its roots lie in the nineteenth century, when workers from New Guinea and nearby islands, recruited for plantations in Samoa and Queensland, needed a common means of communication. The result was a pidgin: a simplified contact language with no native speakers, used mainly for practical purposes. As with many pidgins, most of its vocabulary came from the dominant group's language, here English, but words were also borrowed from German, the colonial language of northern New Guinea until 1914, from the local language Tolai, and from Malay. Its grammar, however, differs markedly from English: possession is expressed with 'bilong', as in 'haus bilong mi' ('my house'), and many verbs that take an object end in '-im'. In a country with more than 800 languages, Tok Pisin gradually spread as a lingua franca in markets, churches and the press and eventually in Parliament. Since the mid-twentieth century, especially in towns where parents from different language groups marry, growing numbers of children have acquired it as their first language. Linguists call this process creolisation: once a pidgin becomes a mother tongue, its vocabulary expands and its grammar grows more elaborate to meet every need of daily life. Tok Pisin thus lets researchers observe in a living language a development that, for many other creoles, can only be reconstructed from historical records.

okuma-dunning-kruger.t: Metacognition, a term psychologists use for the ability to think about one's own thinking, includes the capacity to judge how well one has performed a task. In a set of studies published in 1999, the psychologists Justin Kruger and David Dunning examined how this capacity relates to actual skill. University students took tests of logical reasoning, English grammar and the ability to recognise humour, and then estimated both their raw scores and how their performance compared with that of their peers. Participants whose scores placed them in the bottom quarter performed, on average, better than only about twelve per cent of their classmates, yet they estimated that they had done better than roughly sixty per cent. The researchers argued that the knowledge needed to answer a question correctly is often the same knowledge needed to recognise a correct answer, so those who lack it are poorly placed to notice their own errors. To test this explanation, they gave some participants a short training session in logical reasoning. After the training, the low scorers became noticeably more accurate in assessing the performance they had given earlier, which suggested that improving skill also improved self-evaluation. Top performers made a different kind of mistake: they rated their tests accurately but somewhat underestimated their relative position, apparently assuming that others had found the tasks as easy as they had. The pattern became known as the Dunning–Kruger effect.

okuma-seker-vergisi.t: Drinks that contain large amounts of added sugar are a major source of extra calories in many people's diets. Because high sugar consumption is linked to obesity, type 2 diabetes and tooth decay, several countries have introduced special taxes on these drinks. The idea is simple: if sugary drinks become more expensive, people will buy fewer of them. Mexico, which has one of the highest rates of soft drink consumption in the world, introduced such a tax in 2014. Studies carried out in the following years found that purchases of taxed drinks fell, especially among poorer households. The United Kingdom chose a different approach in 2018, taxing manufacturers according to the amount of sugar in their drinks. Many companies responded by reducing the sugar content of their products before the tax even came into force. Critics argue that such taxes fall most heavily on people with low incomes and that they do little to change overall diets. Supporters reply that poorer families also suffer most from diet-related diseases and therefore stand to benefit most.

okuma-atlantik-telgraf-kablosu.t: In the mid-nineteenth century, news could cross the Atlantic no faster than the ships that carried it. The American financier Cyrus Field set out to change this, founding a company in 1854 with the aim of laying a telegraph cable along the floor of the ocean. The project proved far harder than its supporters had expected. Cables laid in 1857 and in June 1858 broke, and although a line completed that summer allowed Queen Victoria to send a greeting to President James Buchanan, it failed within a few weeks. Public excitement, which had been heightened by lavish celebrations in New York, quickly turned to doubt. Field nevertheless persisted, raising fresh money from investors in London and New York despite the heavy losses that had already been incurred. In 1865 he turned to the Great Eastern, the largest steamship of its day, which was massive enough to carry the entire cable as a single payload; however, this valiant attempt also failed when the line snapped two-thirds of the way across. A year later, the beleaguered enterprise finally succeeded: a new cable linking Valentia in Ireland with Heart's Content in Newfoundland began to operate, and the crew even recovered and completed the cable lost in 1865. Messages could now be transmitted almost immediately along a line submerged deep beneath the waves, an achievement that heralded a new era of global communication.

okuma-bal-arisi.t: When a honeybee finds a good source of food, it returns to the hive and performs a special movement known as the waggle dance. During the dance, the bee walks in a straight line while shaking its body from side to side, then circles back and repeats the movement many times. Other bees gather around the dancer and follow its steps closely. The direction of the straight run tells them where the food is in relation to the sun. If the bee dances straight upwards on the vertical surface of the honeycomb, the food lies in the same direction as the sun. The length of the run, meanwhile, shows how far away the food is: the longer the waggle, the greater the distance. This system was first explained in detail by the Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch, who received a Nobel Prize for his work in 1973. Later studies have shown that the dance is not perfectly precise, so bees that follow it still need to search the area once they arrive. Even so, it allows a colony to send many workers quickly to the richest flowers. For this reason, the waggle dance is often described as one of the most remarkable examples of communication in the animal world.

okuma-mikrobiyom.t: The community of microorganisms that inhabits the human gut, known as the microbiome, is not inherited in the way that genes are; it is assembled anew in each individual, starting at birth. The intestine of an unborn baby is thought to contain few, if any, microbes, and the first colonisers come from the mother and the immediate environment. Infants born vaginally initially acquire bacteria resembling those of the mother's birth canal, whereas those delivered by caesarean section are colonised at first by microbes more typical of the skin and the hospital environment. Diet then plays a decisive role. Human milk contains complex sugars that the infant itself cannot digest; these compounds travel to the large intestine, where they serve as food for particular groups of bacteria, notably species of Bifidobacterium. In this way, breast milk nourishes not only the child but also selected microbial partners. The introduction of solid food brings a rapid increase in diversity, and by the age of about three the gut community has come to resemble that of an adult. Once established, it performs functions that human cells cannot carry out alone. Bacteria ferment dietary fibre into short-chain fatty acids, one of which, butyrate, is a major source of energy for the cells lining the colon, and microbial signals help the developing immune system learn to tolerate harmless substances. Courses of antibiotics, particularly in early childhood, can disturb this community, although it usually recovers at least partly within weeks or months.

okuma-faj.t: As bacteria become increasingly resistant to antibiotics, researchers have revived interest in a treatment that was largely abandoned in the West nearly a century ago. Bacteriophages, or phages, are viruses that infect and destroy bacteria while leaving human cells unharmed. They were discovered in the 1910s, and for a time phage therapy was used to treat conditions such as dysentery. When penicillin and other antibiotics became widely available in the 1940s, however, Western medicine lost interest in phages, partly because antibiotics were easier to produce and acted against a broad range of bacteria. Research continued in the Soviet Union and parts of Eastern Europe, a region where phage therapy is still practised today. One of the main attractions of phages is their specificity: each type typically attacks only one species or even a single strain of bacteria. This means that, unlike broad-spectrum antibiotics, they do not destroy the beneficial microbes that live in the body. Paradoxically, the same feature is also a major drawback, since doctors must identify the exact strain causing an infection and find a phage that matches it, a process that can take days or weeks. Bacteria can also evolve resistance to phages, although phages, which are themselves capable of evolving, can in turn adapt to overcome it. Several well-publicised cases in which patients with life-threatening infections recovered after receiving phages have raised hopes, but such individual successes are no substitute for large controlled trials, which remain scarce. Regulatory systems designed for conventional drugs also struggle to accommodate treatments that may need to be tailored to each patient.

okuma-dijital-ariv.t: Web pages are among the most short-lived records ever produced. Studies of links cited in academic articles and news reports have repeatedly found that a substantial proportion no longer lead to the original content after only a few years, a phenomenon known as 'link rot'. Web archiving attempts to counter this loss. The usual method relies on automated programs called crawlers, which start from a list of addresses, download each page together with its images and style files, and then follow the links they find to further pages. The captured material is stored in a standard container format, together with information recording when and from where each file was collected, so that the page can later be reconstructed as it appeared on a particular date. The largest such collection, begun by a non-profit organisation in San Francisco in 1996, now holds hundreds of billions of captured pages, and many national libraries carry out similar work for websites in their own countries. Nevertheless, the technique has clear limitations. Crawlers struggle with pages whose content is generated by interactive programs or hidden behind login screens, so social media posts and online databases are often captured incompletely or not at all. Moreover, since a page is recorded only at the moment of a visit, any changes made between two visits are lost permanently.

okuma-ahtapot.t: Among invertebrates, the octopus stands out for both the size and the organisation of its nervous system. The common octopus has roughly 500 million neurons, yet only about a third of them are found in the central brain. The remainder are distributed along the eight arms, where clusters of nerve cells coordinate movement and process the information gathered by the suckers. Each sucker is equipped with chemical receptors, so an arm exploring a crevice in a rock can, in effect, taste the surfaces it touches without waiting for instructions from the brain. This arrangement allows an arm to search for prey with a considerable degree of independence while the animal attends to something else. The skin is equally sophisticated. Thousands of pigment-filled cells called chromatophores, each surrounded by tiny muscles, enable the octopus to alter its colour and pattern within a fraction of a second. Strikingly, most octopuses appear to be colour-blind, and researchers are still investigating how they nevertheless manage to match their surroundings so closely. These abilities are all the more remarkable because most octopuses live for only one or two years and receive no care from their parents after hatching. Whatever they know about their environment, they must therefore learn largely on their own and within a single brief lifetime.

okuma-kula-halkasi.t: One of the most influential studies in anthropology is Bronislaw Malinowski's account of the kula, a ceremonial exchange system he observed in the Trobriand Islands and neighbouring parts of the western Pacific. Published in 1922 as Argonauts of the Western Pacific, the work drew on the considerable time he spent living among the islanders and learning their language between 1915 and 1918. At the heart of the kula are two kinds of shell ornaments: necklaces made of red shell and armbands made of white shell. These objects circulate in opposite directions around a ring of islands, often passing between communities that are quite remote from one another. Although socially valuable, the ornaments have little practical use and cannot be exchanged for ordinary goods; Malinowski likens them to a monarchy's crown jewels, prized for their history and associations rather than their usefulness. Even the most cherished pieces are held only for a time before being passed on, and men committed to the kula keep the same partners for life. The exchanges are conducted without bargaining, although ordinary trade in useful goods takes place alongside them. For Malinowski, the kula showed that a seemingly economic activity may in fact be multifaceted, creating prestige and binding together peoples whose relations might otherwise be hostile. His analysis later influenced the French scholar Marcel Mauss, whose famous essay on gift-giving argued that every gift creates an obligation to reciprocate.

okuma-iki-dil.t: Children who hear two languages from birth follow a path of development that is in many ways similar to that of monolingual children, but it has several distinctive features. Newborns whose mothers regularly spoke two languages during pregnancy show interest in both, and within months babies can tell the languages apart by their rhythm and sounds. Around their first birthday, bilingual children usually begin to produce words, at about the same age as children learning a single language. At this stage, their vocabulary is typically divided between the two languages: some objects are named in one language and others in the other, depending on where and with whom the child has heard them. When the words in both languages are counted together, the total is usually comparable to that of monolingual peers, although the vocabulary in each language taken separately may be smaller. Many young bilinguals also combine their languages within a single sentence, a practice known as code-switching. This mixing is not a sign of confusion; it tends to follow grammatical rules and often mirrors the speech habits of the adults around the child. The balance between the two languages can change considerably over time, since it depends largely on how often each one is used at home, at school and among friends.

okuma-lale-cilginligi.b: Bulbs, Contracts and a Sudden Crash
okuma-lale-cilginligi.t: The tulip, a flower native to Central Asia, had long been cultivated in the Ottoman Empire before it reached Western Europe in the sixteenth century. One of the figures most closely linked with its spread is the botanist Carolus Clusius, who planted tulips in the new botanical garden of the University of Leiden in the 1590s. Bulbs soon passed from his garden into private collections, and the flower became a fashionable symbol of wealth in the Dutch Republic. The most prized varieties had petals marked with flame-like streaks of colour. Growers could not reproduce these patterns reliably, and it was not until the twentieth century that scientists discovered that they were caused by a virus spread by aphids, which also weakened the bulbs and slowed their multiplication. The resulting scarcity helped to keep prices high. Because tulips flower only briefly in spring and the bulbs remain underground for most of the year, much of the trade took the form of contracts promising future delivery rather than exchanges of actual bulbs. During the winter of 1636 to 1637, such contracts changed hands repeatedly, often among buyers who never intended to plant the flowers, and prices rose sharply. In early February 1637, buyers at a sale in Haarlem failed to appear, and within days the market collapsed. Many of the contracts were never honoured, and the resulting disputes were settled only slowly.

cloze-suru-bagisikligi.t: When a large proportion of a population is immune to an infectious disease, the disease finds it difficult to spread, (1) ---- there are few people left for it to infect. This indirect protection, known as herd immunity, (2) ---- those who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborn babies and patients with weakened immune systems. The proportion of people who need to be immune (3) ---- from one disease to another. For highly contagious diseases such as measles, around 95 per cent of the population must be protected, (4) ---- for less contagious infections the figure is considerably lower. If vaccination rates fall below this threshold, outbreaks can occur (5) ---- a disease has been rare for many years.

cloze-durtme.t: Traditional economic models assume that people make rational decisions (1) ---- carefully weighing costs and benefits. Behavioural economists, however, have shown that choices are often shaped by seemingly trivial details, such as the order in which options are presented. Building on this insight, some governments have begun to use 'nudges', small changes to the way choices are framed that encourage particular behaviours (2) ---- restricting freedom of choice. For instance, when employees are enrolled in pension schemes automatically and must actively choose to leave, participation rates rise dramatically. Critics, (3) ----, argue that nudging can be manipulative, since it (4) ---- on the very biases it claims to correct. Others point out that the effects of many nudges, (5) ---- impressive in small trials, tend to shrink considerably when they are applied to entire populations.

cloze-tuzdan-arindirma.t: Although more than two thirds of the planet is covered by water, (1) ---- a tiny fraction of it is fresh enough to drink. In dry coastal regions, turning seawater into drinking water has therefore become an attractive option. The most common method today forces seawater at high pressure through a membrane with holes so small that water molecules can pass through (2) ---- salt cannot. The process, known as reverse osmosis, (3) ---- in large plants in the Middle East, Australia and California, some of which produce hundreds of millions of litres a day. Its main (4) ---- is the large amount of energy it requires; although this has fallen considerably over the past two decades, it remains high. Another concern is the salty waste that is returned to the sea, which can harm marine life (5) ---- it is not diluted properly.

cloze-plasebo.t: A placebo is a treatment that contains no active ingredient, such as a sugar pill or an injection of salt water, yet it can still produce measurable improvements in a patient's condition. The key (1) ---- appears to be expectation: when patients believe that a treatment will help them, the brain (2) ---- its own pain-relieving chemicals. Experiments in the late 1970s showed that this response could be blocked by a drug that cancels the effect of the body's natural painkillers, which indicated that the improvement was physical (3) ---- imaginary. The effect tends to be strongest for symptoms such as pain and nausea, which depend heavily on how people perceive their own bodies, and much weaker for conditions that can be measured objectively. (4) ----, a placebo does not shrink tumours or clear infections, so it can support effective treatment but cannot replace it. Some researchers suggest that doctors could make better use of the effect by (5) ---- more time with their patients and explaining treatments in a positive way.

cloze-kan-gruplari.t: Attempts to transfer blood from one person to another were made as early as the seventeenth century, but many of them ended in death, and for a long time the procedure was regarded as too dangerous (1) ---- routine use. The reason was not (2) ---- until 1901, when the Austrian scientist Karl Landsteiner showed that human blood falls into different groups. When blood from an incompatible group is given to a patient, the patient's immune system attacks the donated red cells, (3) ---- a potentially fatal reaction. Landsteiner's discovery made it possible to match donors and recipients (4) ----, and it earned him the Nobel Prize in 1930. Since then, testing blood before a transfusion has gradually become routine, and the safety of the procedure (5) ---- dramatically.

cloze-volkan.t: Around 800 million people live within a hundred kilometres of an active volcano. At first sight, this may seem surprising, (1) ---- the dangers that eruptions pose are well known. However, volcanic regions offer important advantages. Volcanic soils are often exceptionally fertile, (2) ---- them ideal for farming, and the heat beneath the ground can be used to generate electricity. In addition, many people have lived in these areas for generations and are deeply attached to their land. Over recent decades, scientists have become much better at (3) ---- eruptions. By monitoring small earthquakes, changes in the shape of the ground and the gases released from the volcano, they can often detect warning signs days or weeks (4) ----. Such warnings have saved thousands of lives. Nevertheless, forecasts are not always accurate, and authorities must decide whether to evacuate people (5) ---- knowing for certain that an eruption will occur.

cloze-merak.t: In a study published in 2014, researchers at the University of California, Davis examined how curiosity affects memory. Participants first rated how curious they were about the answers to a series of trivia questions. Each question was then shown again, and while participants (1) ---- for the answer to appear, a photograph of an unfamiliar face was briefly displayed. In a later test, participants remembered more of the answers that had aroused their curiosity, and they were also better at (2) ---- the faces shown during those moments, even though the faces had nothing to do with the questions. Brain scans revealed increased activity in reward-related regions and in the hippocampus, a structure that plays a central role in forming new memories. The results suggest that curiosity does not merely make a particular topic more attractive (3) ---- also puts the brain into a state that favours learning in general. Teachers, therefore, (4) ---- from opening a lesson with an intriguing question. Because the participants were tested in a laboratory, however, it remains (5) ---- how strong the effect would be in a crowded classroom.

cloze-kent-bahcesi.t: In many cities, empty plots of land are being turned into community gardens, where local residents grow vegetables, fruit and flowers together. A typical garden is divided into small beds, and each member is (1) ---- for looking after one of them. Members also share tools and water, and they usually meet once a week to (2) ---- the work that the whole garden needs, such as building paths or making compost. The gardens give people a reason to spend time outdoors and help neighbours get to know one another. Research has also shown that green spaces can lower stress levels and (3) ---- local temperatures on hot days. The main difficulty is the land itself, since many gardens do not own the plots they use. (4) ----, they rent them from private owners, who may decide to sell the land to builders. For this reason, gardeners often seek the support of local councils, and in cities where councils have offered long-term leases, some gardens (5) ---- for more than forty years.

s.q: Before the conference, the organisers had all the presentations ---- into three languages.
o: translate
translated
to translate
translating
be translated
s.a: Yapan mı, yapılan mı? have'den sonraki nesne kişi değil şey (the presentations); sunumlar çeviren değil, çevrilen. have + nesne + V3 = yaptırmak: had the presentations translated. translate kişiyle kurulur (had someone translate); to translate ve be translated kalıba uymuyor.

s.q: If the Earth ---- no atmosphere, its average surface temperature ---- far below freezing.
o: has / would have been
had / would be
had had / will be
would have / is
has had / were
s.a: If'in içine bakıyoruz: Dünya'nın atmosferi var, yani bugünkü gerçeğe aykırı hayali bir durum anlatılıyor. Bugünle ilgili hayal: if + V2, ana cümlede would V1, yani had / would be. had had geçmişe ait olurdu ve will ile birleşmez; has gerçek bir koşul kurar, would have been ile uyuşmaz.

s.q: The new hospital is ---- the old one, so it can treat far more patients.
o: as twice large as
twice larger as
twice as large as
large twice than
twice as larger than
s.a: Kat bildiren karşılaştırma kalıbı: twice / three times + as + sıfat + as. Yeni hastane eskisinin iki katı büyüklükte: twice as large as. Diğer şıklar ya kalıbın sırasını bozuyor ya da than ile as … as yapısını karıştırıyor; "so it can treat far more patients" anlamı doğruluyor.

s.q: The government agreed to fund the archaeological excavation ---- all artefacts recovered from the site would remain in the national museum rather than being sent abroad.
o: in spite of
even though
whereas
as a result of
on condition that
s.a: Boşluktan sonra ne geliyor? Tam bir cümle (all artefacts … would remain); isim alan in spite of ve as a result of gidiyor. Hükûmet desteği bir şarta bağlıyor, eserler ülkede kalacak: on condition that (… şartıyla). even though ve whereas zıtlık kurar, burada zıtlık yok.

s.q: The government has decided ---- construction of the dam until a full environmental assessment ----.
o: postponing / is completing
to be postponed / completed
to postpone / has been completed
postpone / will have completed
having postponed / had completed
s.a: decide fiilden sonra to V1 ile devam eder: decided to postpone. İkinci boşluk until'den sonra: zaman bağlacının içinde will olmaz, gelecekte tamamlanacak iş present perfect ile anlatılır. Değerlendirme tamamlayan değil tamamlanan: has been completed. postponing ve postpone decide kalıbını bozuyor.

s.q: ---- bridges are designed to bend slightly in strong winds instead of resisting them completely, tall buildings in earthquake zones are built on flexible foundations that allow them to sway.
o: Just as
Unless
Even though
As if
Until
s.a: Boşluktan sonra tam cümle var. İki taraf aynı fikri iki yapı için söylüyor: köprüler rüzgârda esniyor, binalar depremde salınıyor. Benzerliği Just as (tıpkı … gibi) kuruyor. Even though zıtlık, Unless koşul, As if gerçek dışı benzetme, Until zaman bildirir.

s.q: ---- the Moon has no atmosphere to protect it, its surface is covered with craters formed by objects that would have burnt up before reaching the Earth.
o: Although
Because
Unless
Whereas
As if
s.a: Boşluktan sonra tam cümle var, bağlaç başta; şıkların hepsi cümle alıyor. Atmosfer yok (eksi), yüzey kraterlerle kaplı (eksi). Eksi-eksi paralel yapı: sebep-sonuç, Because. Although ve Whereas zıtlık, Unless koşul, As if benzetme kurar.

s.q: Linguists are trying to understand the reasons ---- some languages survive for centuries while others disappear within a few generations.
o: which
how
whose
whom
why
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "some languages survive…" tam bir cümle; özne de yüklem de yerinde. Önündeki isim "the reasons": sebep + tam cümle, why (dillerin yaşayıp yok olma nedenleri). which ve whom eksik cümle ister, whose arkasından isim ister; how ise reasons ile kalıp kurmaz.

s.q: Many travellers in the Middle Ages carried letters of introduction from local officials ---- they were stopped and questioned by the authorities of a foreign town.
o: although
unless
as if
in case
whereas
s.a: Boşluktan sonra tam cümle var. Bir yanda olası bir durum (yabancı kentte durdurulup sorgulanmak), öbür yanda ona karşı alınan tedbir (tanıtım mektubu taşımak): in case (… olur diye). although ve whereas zıtlık, unless koşul, as if benzetme bildirir.

s.q: ---- the considerable cost of the equipment, many hospitals have adopted robotic surgery because it shortens recovery times for patients.
o: Because of
Rather than
With the exception of
As a result of
Notwithstanding
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "the considerable cost" bir isim; şıkların hepsi isim alıyor. Artı-eksi: ekipman çok pahalı (eksi), yine de benimsenmiş (artı); zıtlık: Notwithstanding (= despite). Because of ve As a result of maliyeti sebep yapar; sebep zaten "because it shortens" ile verilmiş.

s.q: ---- the new currency was introduced, prices rose sharply and many people lost their savings.
o: When
Unless
Although
Whereas
As if
s.a: Önce yapı: boşluktan sonra geçmiş zamanlı tam cümle, ana cümle de past; zaman uyumu tutuyor. Yeni para birimi gelince fiyatlar fırladı: art arda iki geçmiş olay, zaman ilişkisi: When. Although ve Whereas zıtlık ister; Unless koşul, As if benzetme bildirir.

s.q: ---- its well-known role in digestion, the liver also stores several essential vitamins and removes toxic substances from the blood before they reach other organs.
o: Except for
Instead of
Apart from
Because of
As opposed to
s.a: İpucu ana cümledeki "also": karaciğerin bilinen rolüne bir işlev daha ekleniyor. Apart from burada in addition to (… -in yanı sıra) anlamında. Except for yalnız "hariç" demektir, ekleme yapmaz; Because of, Instead of ve As opposed to da also ile bu eklemeyi kurmaz.

s.q: There is ---- evidence that the herbal remedy actually works, yet it remains popular in many countries.
o: few
little
many
a few
a little
s.a: evidence sayılamaz; few, a few ve many anlama girmeden gidiyor. yet zıtlık istiyor: bir tarafta popülerlik (artı), öbür tarafta kanıt eksi olmalı. little = çok az (eksi), a little = biraz (artı); zıtlığı little kuruyor.

s.q: Wind turbines can convert only part of the energy carried by moving air into electricity; ----, a considerable share of that energy passes through the blades without being captured.
o: however
for instance
instead
in other words
otherwise
s.a: Noktalı virgülden sonra 4. grup bağlaç var. İki taraf da eksi ve aynı bilgiyi veriyor: enerjinin yalnız bir kısmı ("only part") dönüşüyor, büyük payı yakalanmadan geçiyor. Aynı fikri açan in other words (yani). however zıtlık ister; for instance örnek, otherwise "aksi hâlde" bildirir.

s.q: ---- of the samples collected from the river contained traces of heavy metals, which worried local officials.
o: Much
Every
Most
Little
A great deal
s.a: Arkadaki isim "the samples": sayılabilir çoğul ve belirli bir grup. most of the + sayılabilir çoğul: Most of the samples (örneklerin çoğu). Much, Little ve A great deal sayılamayanla gider; Every ise tekil isim alır ve of ile kullanılmaz.

s.q: It remains a subject of debate exactly ---- the first humans reached the Americas.
o: that
what
which
when
whom
s.a: Baştaki It, boşlukla başlayan isim cümlesinin yerini tutuyor. Boşluktan sonra "the first humans reached the Americas" tam bir cümle; what, which ve whom eksik cümle ister. "a subject of debate" bir belirsizlik anlatıyor ve tartışılan zaman: exactly when (tam olarak ne zaman). that belirsizlik değil bilgi verir.

s.q: The mineral was first discovered near the village of Ytterby in Sweden, ---- the name yttrium given to the element that was later extracted from it.
o: hence
while
since
after
as
s.a: Boşluktan sonra cümle değil, isim öbeği var (the name yttrium given to …). hence isim öbeğiyle de gelir ve sonucu bildirir: köyün adı Ytterby, elementin adı da buradan geliyor. while, since, after ve as bu yapıda sonuç anlamı vermez.

s.q: When ---- to direct sunlight for long periods, some medicines lose their effectiveness.
o: exposing
having exposed
exposed
to expose
expose
s.a: When'den sonra sadeleşmiş yapı geliyor; özneler ortak: ilaçlar. İlaçlar güneşe maruz bırakan mı, bırakılan mı? Bırakılan; boşluktan sonra nesne yok, "to direct sunlight" edatla geliyor. Pasif için V3: When exposed. exposing ve having exposed aktif, to expose ve expose ise sadeleştirme yapısına uymuyor.

s.q: In the nineteenth century, many factory owners would not ---- their workers take breaks during shifts that lasted up to fourteen hours.
o: let
allow
permit
get
want
s.a: Nesneden (their workers) sonra yalın V1 geliyor: take. Yalın V1 alan ettirgen fiiller let ve make; izin anlamını let veriyor. allow, permit, get ve want aynı yerde to V1 ister (allow them to take).

s.q: Although the second experiment was designed more carefully, its results were ---- reliable than those of the first.
o: not as
the least
no more
as much
so much
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "reliable than" var; than ile more / less ya da no more kurulur. Although zıtlık istiyor: deney daha dikkatli tasarlanmış (artı), sonuçlar ise ilkinden hiç de güvenilir değil (eksi): no more reliable than. not as ve as much ikinci bir as ister; the least ve so much than ile kullanılmaz.

s.q: Critics warn that the new policy will ---- existing inequalities rather than reduce them, as its benefits will go mainly to wealthier households.
o: alleviate
exacerbate
postpone
commemorate
verify
s.a: Bağlaç rather than, yani zıtlık: politika eşitsizlikleri azaltmak yerine onun tersini yapacak. as ile gelen sebep de bunu doğruluyor: faydalar çoğunlukla varlıklı hanelere gidecek. Eşitsizliği derinleştirmek: exacerbate (kötüleştirmek). alleviate (hafifletmek) "reduce" ile aynı yönde, zıtlığı bozuyor.

s.q: The ---- of obesity among children has risen sharply over the past three decades, prompting health authorities in many countries to launch programmes that promote healthy eating.
o: tolerance
confidentiality
compliance
prevalence
coherence
s.a: Problem–önlem kalıbı: sağlık kurumları sağlıklı beslenme programları başlatmış (önlem); o hâlde çocuklarda "has risen sharply" ile artan şey bir sorun. Bir hastalığın toplumda ne kadar yaygın olduğunu prevalence (yaygınlık) verir. tolerance (hoşgörü) ve compliance (uyum) obeziteyle eşdizim kurmuyor.

s.q: Many coastal towns are highly ---- to flooding, as they are built on low-lying land close to the sea.
o: resistant
vulnerable
immune
superior
indifferent
s.a: Buradaki as "çünkü" anlamında: kasabalar denize yakın, alçak arazide kurulmuş; bu sel karşısında bir zayıflık (eksi). Sebep eksi, sonuç da eksi olmalı: vulnerable to (… karşısında savunmasız). resistant (dayanıklı) da to alır ama alçak arazi dayanıklılığı değil zayıflığı açıklar; yön ters.

s.q: The museum's collection is so ---- that visitors can see everything from ancient pottery to contemporary video installations.
o: fragile
diverse
obscure
redundant
hostile
s.a: Boşluktan sonra so … that sonucu geliyor: ziyaretçiler antik çömlekten çağdaş video enstalasyonlarına kadar her şeyi görebiliyor. "from … to" ile verilen bu geniş yelpaze çeşitliliği anlatıyor: diverse (çeşitli). fragile (kırılgan) ve obscure (az bilinen) bu sonucu doğurmuyor.

s.q: Although the two species look almost identical, genetic analysis has revealed that they ---- from a common ancestor more than ten million years ago.
o: refrained
abstained
dissuaded
diverged
retreated
s.a: Although zıtlık istiyor: iki tür neredeyse aynı görünüyor (benzerlik), genetik analiz ise bir farklılık ortaya koymalı. "from a common ancestor … ten million years ago" ortak atadan ayrılmayı anlatıyor: diverged (ayrıldı). refrained ve abstained da from alır ama "kaçınmak" demek; burada edat değil anlam eliyor.

s.q: Despite the economic crisis, the number of tourists visiting the country has remained ---- stable over the past five years.
o: hardly
relatively
eagerly
deliberately
mutually
s.a: Despite zıtlık kuruyor: ekonomik kriz eksi, öbür tarafta bir artı arıyoruz. Zarf "stable" sıfatını niteliyor; "ne kadar sabit?" diye soruyoruz: relatively (görece). hardly (neredeyse hiç) sabitliği ortadan kaldırıp iki tarafı da eksi yapar, zıtlık bozulur; eagerly ve deliberately sıfatla anlam kurmuyor.

s.q: The government has promised to ---- the gap between rich and poor regions by investing in roads, schools and hospitals in the least developed parts of the country.
o: widen
measure
narrow
justify
disguise
s.a: Yöntemi by + V-ing veriyor: en az gelişmiş bölgelere yol, okul ve hastane yatırımı. Yoksul bölgelere yatırım aradaki farkı kapatır: narrow the gap. widen the gap de sık bir eşdizim ama yatırımın yönüne ters; measure, justify ve disguise bir yatırımın sonucu olamaz.

s.q: Rather than being a sudden event, the collapse of the empire was a ---- process that unfolded over several centuries.
o: abrupt
instantaneous
protracted
reciprocal
tentative
s.a: Rather than zıtlık kuruyor: çöküş "a sudden event" (ani bir olay) değil, onun tersi; sağdaki "over several centuries" de yüzyıllara yayılan bir süreç anlatıyor. Bunu protracted (uzun süren, uzayıp giden) karşılıyor. abrupt ve instantaneous "ani" demek, yani dışarıda bırakılan anlamı tekrar ediyor.

s.q: The survey revealed a ---- decline in public trust in the media over the past decade, with the share of respondents who said they believed what they read in newspapers falling from nearly two thirds to fewer than one in three.
o: deliberate
striking
negligible
reversible
seasonal
s.a: Boşluğun sağ tarafı belirleyici: gazetelere güvenenlerin oranı üçte ikiden üçte birin altına inmiş; düşüş çok büyük. Bunu niteleyen sıfat striking (çarpıcı). negligible düşüşü önemsiz gösteriyor, yön ters; seasonal on yıllık eğilime, deliberate kamu güvenine uymuyor, reversible parçada dayanaksız.

s.q: Smoking during pregnancy has been shown to ---- the growth of the unborn baby and to increase the likelihood of premature birth and low birth weight.
o: enhance
impair
aid
assemble
endorse
s.a: Bağlaç and, yani paralel yapı: ikinci tarafta "increase the likelihood of premature birth and low birth weight" eksi; o hâlde boşluk da eksi olmalı. Hamilelikte sigara bebeğin büyümesine zarar veriyor: impair (bozmak, sekteye uğratmak). enhance (artırmak) ve aid (desteklemek) artı yönlü, paralel yapıyı bozuyor.

s.q: The findings are ----, since the study involved only twenty participants and lacked a control group.
o: unprecedented
inconclusive
indisputable
comprehensive
compelling
s.a: Buradaki since "çünkü" anlamında ve sebep eksi: "only twenty participants" ve "lacked a control group". Eksi-eksi paralel yapı: sebep eksiyse sonuç da eksi olmalı. Bulgular kesin bir sonuca götürmüyor: inconclusive. indisputable (tartışılmaz) ve compelling (ikna edici) artı yönlü, eleniyor.

s.q: Her research ---- a new approach to the study of ancient languages, one that relies on computer analysis and has since been adopted by scholars around the world.
o: pioneered
abandoned
resisted
discredited
concealed
s.a: Sağ taraf belirleyici: yaklaşım "has since been adopted by scholars around the world"; "new" de bir ilki gösteriyor: pioneered (öncülük etti). abandoned, resisted ve discredited yaygın kabulle çelişiyor; concealed benimsenen bir yaklaşıma uymuyor.

s.q: The government plans to ---- a tax on sugary drinks in an effort to reduce obesity among children.
o: impose
comprise
evade
inhibit
deprive
s.a: Amaç bölümü ipucu: "in an effort to reduce obesity", yani hükûmet şekerli içecek tüketimini azaltmak istiyor. "a tax" ile kurulan ve bu amaca hizmet eden kalıp impose a tax (vergi koymak). evade a tax (vergiden kaçmak) da bir eşdizim ama vergiyi koyanın değil, ödemesi gerekenin işi ve amaca ters.

s.q: Although the evidence is largely ----, it strongly suggests that the treatment is effective.
o: conclusive
abundant
anecdotal
rigorous
compelling
s.a: Although zıtlık istiyor: ana cümle artı, "strongly suggests that the treatment is effective". O hâlde kanıtın niteliği eksi olmalı: anecdotal (kişisel anlatılara dayanan, sistemli olmayan). conclusive, rigorous ve compelling artı yönlü; iki tarafı da artı yapar, zıtlık kurulmaz.

s.q: A new dating technique that measures the decay of certain elements has made it possible to ---- the age of volcanic rocks with far greater accuracy than earlier methods allowed.
o: determine
overstate
disguise
preserve
alter
s.a: Boşluğun sağ tarafı belirleyici: nesne "the age of volcanic rocks", ardından "with far greater accuracy". Doğrulukla yapılan iş bir saptamadır: determine (belirlemek). overstate (abartmak) doğrulukla çelişiyor; preserve, alter ve disguise bir ölçüm tekniğinin işi değil.

s.q: The museum's decision to return the artefacts to their country of origin has been ---- as a significant step towards addressing historical injustices.
o: dismissed
criticised
inhibited
concealed
hailed
s.a: Sağda "as a significant step towards addressing historical injustices" var: karar tarihsel haksızlıkları gidermede önemli bir adım sayılıyor, cümle artı. be + V3 + as kalıbında övgü bildiren hailed (… olarak alkışlandı) oturuyor. dismissed ve criticised da as alır ama yön ters.

s.q: The independent review ---- several serious weaknesses in the country's emergency services, including slow response times and a shortage of trained staff.
o: concealed
highlighted
prevented
resolved
tolerated
s.a: Sağ taraf belirleyici: "including slow response times and a shortage of trained staff", değerlendirme zayıflıkları tek tek sayıyor: highlighted (dikkat çekti). concealed sayılan zayıflıklarla çelişiyor; resolved ve prevented bir raporun değil, uygulamanın işi.

s.q: Patients who do not ---- with their treatment, for example by skipping doses or stopping their medicine as soon as they feel better, are far more likely to be readmitted to hospital.
o: interfere
coincide
comply
sympathise
negotiate
s.a: Boşluğun sağında "for example by skipping doses" var: doz atlamak ve iyi hissedince ilacı bırakmak tedaviye uymamanın örnekleri. Tedaviye uymak: comply with. Şıkların hepsi with alıyor, edat bir şey elemiyor; coincide ve interfere tedaviyle bu anlamı kurmuyor.

s.q: The committee was criticised for its ---- to act, as it delayed its decision on the proposal for more than two years despite repeated warnings from experts.
o: capacity
reluctance
tendency
eagerness
determination
s.a: Kökteki "was criticised for" eleştirilecek, eksi bir şey istiyor; as ile gelen sebep de bunu veriyor: komite uyarılara rağmen kararı iki yıldan fazla geciktirmiş. Harekete geçmekte isteksizlik: reluctance to act. eagerness (heves) ve determination (kararlılık) artı yönlü, hem eleştiriye hem gecikmeye ters.

s.q: Because many of the chemical reactions that take place inside a rechargeable battery are ----, the products can be turned back into the original substances each time the battery is charged.
o: volatile
spontaneous
exothermic
insoluble
reversible
s.a: Because sebep-sonuç kuruyor; sonuçta ürünler her şarjda "turned back into the original substances", yani başlangıç maddelerine dönüyor. Geri döndürülebilen tepkime reversible (tersinir). exothermic (ısı veren), spontaneous (kendiliğinden), volatile (uçucu) ve insoluble (çözünmez) geri dönüşü açıklamıyor.

s.q: Whereas earlier research focused almost exclusively on the genetic causes of the disease, ----.
o: the disease was first described in detail by a French physician in 1872
recent studies have paid more attention to environmental factors such as diet
genes are passed from parents to their children in a predictable way
researchers have identified several genes that are closely linked to the disease
many patients do not show any symptoms of the disease until later in life
s.a: Whereas karşılaştırma kurar: kökte "earlier research" genetik nedenlere odaklanmış. Hem zaman hem konu zıtlığı arıyoruz: recent studies have paid more attention to environmental factors such as diet. Gen şıkkı genetik tarafta kalıyor, zıtlık kurmuyor; 1872 şıkkı konu-limit dışı.

s.q: Because the government's income comes almost entirely from oil exports, ----.
o: the country has been able to develop a wide range of other industries
its budget is largely protected from changes in world oil prices
oil was first discovered in the country in the early twentieth century
a sharp fall in world oil prices can quickly force cuts in public spending
rising oil prices usually force the government to raise taxes
s.a: Because sebep-sonuç kuruyor; kökte eksi bir bağımlılık var: gelir neredeyse tamamen petrolden. Eksi-eksi paralel sonuç: a sharp fall in world oil prices can quickly force cuts in public spending. Bütçenin korunması ve vergi artışı yorumu ters çeviriyor; petrolün ilk bulunuşu sebebe bağlanmıyor.

s.q: If governments want young people to stay in rural areas, ----.
o: young people have moved to the cities in large numbers
they will have to create jobs and improve services there
many villages will continue to lose their young population
farming would no longer be the main source of income there
the cities will offer far more opportunities than the countryside
s.a: If + present (want) → ana cümlede will ya da modal + V1; present perfect ve would taşıyan şıklar yapıca gidiyor. Kökte bir amaç var, cevapta yapılması gerekeni arıyoruz: they will have to create jobs and improve services there. Köylerin boşalması amacın tersi; kentlerin fırsatları bir önlem değil.

s.q: Many adults who start a foreign language course drop out within the first few months ----.
o: so that they can practise speaking with native speakers more often
although learning a language is widely regarded as a lifelong process
whereas children usually acquire the pronunciation of a new language more easily
because they expect to make faster progress than is realistic and soon become discouraged
as long as the course fees are paid in advance
s.a: Kökte eksi bir davranış var: birçok yetişkin kursu ilk aylarda bırakıyor. Sebebini arıyoruz, eksi-eksi paralel yapı: because they expect … and soon become discouraged. although şıkkında uzun süreç bırakmayı destekliyor, zıtlık yok; so that, whereas ve as long as bırakmayla bağ kurmuyor.

s.q: Since the enzyme works only within a narrow range of temperatures, ----.
o: it is found in almost every living organism on the planet
it was first isolated from bacteria living in hot springs
the reaction slows down considerably if the mixture is allowed to cool
the researchers were surprised by how quickly it broke down the sample
it can be stored at room temperature for several years without any loss of activity
s.a: Since burada "çünkü": enzim "only within a narrow range of temperatures" çalışıyor. Bu sınırın sonucunu arıyoruz: the reaction slows down considerably if the mixture is allowed to cool. Oda sıcaklığında saklama şıkkı sıcaklıkla ilgili ama sonuç değil; kaynak ve yaygınlık şıkları konu-limit dışı.

s.q: ----, the findings suggest that the benefits of the treatment may have been overestimated.
o: Since the treatment has been used successfully for decades
As the earlier studies confirmed the benefits beyond doubt
Because the patients recovered much faster than expected
While the earlier studies reported dramatic improvements
Provided that the treatment is given at an early stage
s.a: Kökte eksi bir bulgu var: faydalar "may have been overestimated". Artı bir bilgiyle zıtlık arıyoruz: While the earlier studies reported dramatic improvements. While önce zıtlık olarak okunur. Since, As ve Because ile başlayan şıklar artı sebep veriyor, eksi sonuçla paralel değil.

s.q: Doctors usually advise people to keep a minor wound clean and covered ----.
o: since a wound that is left uncovered tends to heal without leaving a scar
although bacteria can enter an open wound within minutes of an injury
because covering a wound prevents the skin from getting the air it needs to heal
so that bacteria from the surrounding environment cannot easily enter it
until the bacteria inside it have been destroyed by antibiotics
s.a: Kökte bir tavsiye var: yarayı temiz ve kapalı tutmak. Tavsiyenin amacını so that veriyor: so that bacteria from the surrounding environment cannot easily enter it. although şıkkı tavsiyenin sebebini zıtlıkla bağlıyor; açık yaranın iz bırakmadığını ya da havaya ihtiyaç duyduğunu söyleyen şıklar tavsiyeyle çelişiyor.

s.q: So rapidly did the city expand during the nineteenth century ----.
o: that its population is expected to double over the next thirty years
that many of its historic buildings have survived until today
that its sewage systems could not keep pace with its population
that the railway finally reached it in the early 1840s
that new housing is rarely built on the outskirts of the city today
s.a: Başta so + zarf + yardımcı fiil + özne … that kalıbı var; bütün şıklar that ile başlıyor, yapı eleme yapmıyor. Hızlı büyümenin sonucunu arıyoruz: that its sewage systems could not keep pace with its population. Demiryolunun gelişi sebep olabilir, sonuç değil; gelecekteki nüfus 19. yüzyıla bağlanmaz.

s.q: Some historians argue that the Industrial Revolution began in Britain not because of any single invention but ----.
o: although several inventors in other European countries made very similar discoveries
so that British factories could compete with the textile producers of India and China
whereas the steam engine was greatly improved by James Watt in the 1770s
as long as coal remained the most important source of energy in the country
because a particular combination of cheap coal and high wages made machines profitable there
s.a: Kökte "not because of any single invention but" görüyoruz: not … but iki tarafı aynı türden ister. İlk taraf sebep, o hâlde but'tan sonra da sebep gelir: because a particular combination of cheap coal and high wages made machines profitable there. although, so that, whereas ve as long as sebep bildirmez.

s.q: Unlike earlier epidemics, which spread slowly along trade routes, ----.
o: the plague killed a large proportion of the population of Europe in the fourteenth century
doctors in the Middle Ages had little understanding of how diseases were transmitted
trade routes connected Asia with Europe for many centuries
modern outbreaks can reach distant continents within days because of air travel
some diseases are transmitted by insects rather than by people
s.a: Unlike karşılaştırma kurar: eski salgınlar ticaret yollarında "slowly" yayıldı. Karşıt tarafı arıyoruz: modern outbreaks can reach distant continents within days because of air travel. Veba şıkkı kendisi eski bir salgın, karşılaştırma kurmuyor; diğer şıklar konu-limit dışı.

s.q: Public libraries in many towns now lend laptops and tablets as well as books, ----.
o: although they have lent books to the public for well over a century
unless borrowers return them within two weeks
because printed books have become far more expensive in recent years
so people who cannot afford these devices can still use the internet for study and work
whereas many libraries have also reduced their opening hours
s.a: Kökte artı bir hizmet var: kütüphaneler kitabın yanında dizüstü ve tablet de veriyor. so ile sonucunu arıyoruz: so people who cannot afford these devices can still use the internet. although ve whereas zıtlık kurar ama zıtlık yok; kitap fiyatları şıkkı tablet vermeyi açıklamıyor.

s.q: Whereas acute pain usually disappears once an injury has healed, ----.
o: it is often treated with simple painkillers such as paracetamol
chronic pain can persist for years after the original cause has gone
the injury is more common in elderly patients
doctors are able to measure it accurately with a special scanner
patients often describe it as a sharp or burning feeling
s.a: Whereas karşılaştırma kurar: akut ağrı yara iyileşince "disappears". Karşıt ağrı türünü ve karşıt durumu arıyoruz: chronic pain can persist for years after the original cause has gone. Diğer şıklar yine akut ağrı ya da yara hakkında bilgi veriyor, karşılaştırma kurmuyor.

s.q: Now that the course is offered online as well as on campus, ----.
o: students who live far from the university can attend it without having to move
it had attracted more applicants than any other course at the university
the university has to rent larger lecture halls to hold all the students
students who attend it in person tend to achieve slightly higher marks
the number of places on campus was reduced to save money
s.a: Now that (-dığına göre, artık) yeni bir durumun sonucunu sorar; kök present, sonuç da bugüne bağlanır. Ders çevrim içi de verildiğine göre uzaktaki öğrenci taşınmadan katılabilir: students who live far from the university can attend it without having to move. Büyük salon ihtiyacı yorumu ters; past perfect şık zamana uymuyor.

s.q: If you want to improve your vocabulary in a foreign language, ----.
o: you will find that grammar is harder to learn than vocabulary
learning new words would have been much easier as a child
you should read widely and note down the new words you meet
memorising long lists of words had been the most effective method
many learners forget most new words within a few days
s.a: If + present (want) → ana cümlede will ya da modal + V1; would have ve had V3 taşıyan şıklar yapıca gidiyor. İstek bir amaç, cevapta öneri arıyoruz: you should read widely and note down the new words you meet. Unutma oranını veren şık bilgi cümlesi; dil bilgisi şıkkı limit dışı.

s.q: Even though the two metals look very similar, ----.
o: they are both widely used in the construction industry
neither of them is found in its pure form in nature
both conduct electricity better than most metals
they are often mixed to produce a stronger alloy
their melting points differ by several hundred degrees
s.a: Even though zıtlık istiyor; kökte benzerlik var: iki metal "look very similar". Benzerliğin karşısında farklılık arıyoruz: their melting points differ by several hundred degrees. both, neither ve alaşım şıkları yine ortaklık anlatıyor, zıtlık kurmuyor.

s.q: Many historians argue that the spread of the railways transformed nineteenth-century society, ----.
o: although the railways made travel cheaper and faster than ever before
since they allowed people and goods to move far more quickly than ever before
unless the first lines were built with government money
whereas the first public railway opened in Britain in the 1820s
so that most people still rarely travelled beyond their home towns
s.a: Kökte bir iddia var: demiryolları 19. yüzyıl toplumunu dönüştürdü. İddianın sebebini arıyoruz: since they allowed people and goods to move far more quickly (since = çünkü). although şıkkı benzer bilgiyi zıtlık gibi sunuyor, oysa artı-artı; so that şıkkı dönüşümle çelişiyor.

s.q: Many of the world's largest cities are located on coasts or rivers, ----.
o: whereas trade has always depended on easy access to water
unless they are protected from the wind by high mountains
so that it is easier for engineers to build skyscrapers there
although water is essential for human survival
which makes them especially vulnerable to rising sea levels and flooding
s.a: Kökte bir bilgi var: büyük şehirler kıyıda ya da nehir kenarında. Virgülden sonra bütün cümleye gönderme yapıp sonucunu veren which arıyoruz: which makes them especially vulnerable to rising sea levels and flooding. whereas ve although zıtlık kurar ama ortada zıtlık yok; so that amaç bildirir.

s.q: Researchers found that patients who received the new therapy recovered more quickly, ----.
o: since the therapy had not yet been approved by the national health authorities
unless they had been given the standard treatment for several weeks
but they also reported more side effects than the control group
whereas the therapy had been developed by a team of scientists in Canada
so that the standard treatment had been completely abandoned
s.a: Kökte artı bir bulgu var: hastalar "recovered more quickly". Cevapta eksi bir yan arıyoruz: but they also reported more side effects than the control group. Artı-eksi zıtlığını but kuruyor. whereas şıkkında zıtlık yok; since, unless ve so that iyileşmeyle bağ kurmuyor.

s.q: ----; therefore, the final match of the season was postponed until the following week.
o: Heavy overnight rain had left the pitch completely waterlogged
Several key players had recovered from their injuries just in time
The match is expected to attract a record number of spectators
Tickets for the rearranged match will go on sale on Monday
The referee had already inspected the pitch and declared it fit for play
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "; therefore" geliyor: boşluk ertelemenin sebebi olmalı, ana cümle past olduğu için sebep de past ya da past perfect. Eksi-eksi: Heavy overnight rain had left the pitch completely waterlogged. Sahanın uygun bulunması ve oyuncuların iyileşmesi yorumu ters; present ve future şıklar zamana uymuyor.

s.q: The more time children spend reading for pleasure, ----.
o: the more books are published for young readers every year
they are encouraged by teachers to visit libraries
reading aloud was common in many families in the past
so their parents may buy them electronic devices
the wider their vocabulary tends to become
s.a: The more …, the + karşılaştırma kalıbı: ikinci yarı da the + -er/more ile başlar. Çocuklar keyif için okudukça kelime dağarcıklarının genişlediğini görüyoruz; their de çocuklara gidiyor: the wider their vocabulary tends to become. Yayımlanan kitap şıkkı kalıba uysa da sonucu çocuklarda değil, yayın piyasasında arıyor.

s.q: Gothic cathedrals could have far larger windows than earlier Romanesque churches because flying buttresses carried much of the weight of the stone vaults away from the walls.
o: Taş tonozların ağırlığının büyük bölümünü duvarlardan uzağa aktaran uçan payandalar, Gotik katedrallerde daha önceki Romanesk kiliselerdekinden çok daha büyük olabiliyordu.
Uçan payandalar taş tonozların ağırlığının büyük bölümünü duvarlardan uzağa aktardığı için Gotik katedrallerin pencereleri, daha önceki Romanesk kiliselerinkinden çok daha büyük olabiliyordu.
Gotik katedrallerin pencereleri daha önceki Romanesk kiliselerinkinden çok daha büyük olabildiğinden uçan payandalar, taş tonozların ağırlığının büyük bölümünü duvarlardan uzağa aktarıyordu.
Uçan payandalar taş tonozların ağırlığının büyük bölümünü duvarlardan uzağa aktardığı için Gotik katedraller, daha önceki Romanesk kiliselerin pencerelerinden çok daha büyük olabiliyordu.

s.a: Karşılaştırılan iki öğe pencereler: "far larger windows than earlier Romanesque churches" (Romanesk kiliselerinkinden çok daha büyük); because sebebi payandalara bağlıyor. "olabildiğinden … aktarıyordu" diyen şık sebep-sonucu ters kuruyor; "katedraller … pencerelerinden büyük" diyen şık karşılaştırmayı yanlış öğeye kuruyor.

s.q: Dünyadaki tarım bitkilerinin genetik çeşitliliğini savaşlara ve doğal afetlere karşı korumak amacıyla Norveç'e bağlı Svalbard Takımadaları'nda bir dağın içine inşa edilen Küresel Tohum Deposu, bugün bir milyondan fazla tohum örneği barındırmaktadır.
o: Built into a mountain on Norway's Svalbard archipelago to protect the genetic diversity of the world's crops against wars and natural disasters, the Global Seed Vault today holds more than a million seed samples.

The Global Seed Vault, which today holds more than a million seed samples, was built into a mountain on Norway's Svalbard archipelago to protect the genetic diversity of the world's crops against wars and natural disasters.
Built in Svalbard, the Global Seed Vault today holds more than a million seed samples, which protects the genetic diversity of the world's crops against wars and natural disasters.

Norway, which built the Global Seed Vault into a mountain on its Svalbard archipelago to protect the genetic diversity of the world's crops against wars and natural disasters, today holds more than a million seed samples.

Built into a mountain on Norway's Svalbard archipelago against wars and natural disasters, the Global Seed Vault, which protects the genetic diversity of more than a million of the world's crops, today holds their seed samples.
s.a: Yüklem sonda: "barındırmaktadır" = holds. Özne uzun bir sıfat-fiille nitelenmiş: "korumak amacıyla … inşa edilen" = Built … to protect …. Doğru şık bu öbeği başa alıp "the Global Seed Vault today holds …" diyor. "which today holds" diyen şık ana yüklemi ilgi cümlesine indiriyor; "Norway" ile başlayan şık özneyi değiştiriyor.

s.q: Many workers who moved to cities during the Industrial Revolution lived in crowded housing that lacked clean water.
o: Sanayi Devrimi sırasında kentlere göç eden birçok işçi, temiz sudan yoksun kalabalık konutlarda yaşamıştır.
Sanayi Devrimi sırasında temiz sudan yoksun kalabalık konutlarda yaşayan birçok işçi, kentlere göç etmiştir.
Sanayi Devrimi sırasında kentlere göç eden işçilerin tamamı, yalnızca temiz sudan değil elektrikten de yoksun kalabalık konutlarda yaşamıştır.
Sanayi Devrimi sırasında kentlere göç eden birçok işçi, kalabalık konutlarda yaşadığından temiz sudan yoksun kalmıştır.
Sanayi Devrimi sırasında işçilerin göç ettiği kentler, temiz sudan yoksun kalabalık konutlarla dolmuştur.
s.a: Özne "Many workers who moved to cities" (kentlere göç eden birçok işçi), yüklem "lived" (yaşamıştır), "that lacked clean water" konutları niteliyor. Doğru şık bu yapıyı koruyan cümle. En güçlü çeldirici yüklemlerin yerini değiştiriyor; ana yüklem "göç etmiştir" olmuş.

s.q: Ordularını uzun seferlerde besleyebilmek için yiyecekleri bozulmadan saklamanın bir yolunu arayan Fransız hükûmetinin ödülünü kazanan Nicolas Appert, gıdaları cam kavanozlara koyup hava almayacak biçimde kapattıktan sonra kaynar suda ısıtarak konserveciliğin temelini atmıştır.
o: Nicolas Appert, who was looking for a way to preserve food without it spoiling so that the French government could feed its armies on long campaigns, won its prize by putting food into glass jars and heating them in boiling water after sealing them airtight, which laid the foundations of canning.

Nicolas Appert, who won the prize offered by the French government, which was looking for a way to preserve food without it spoiling so as to feed its armies on long campaigns, laid the foundations of canning by putting food into glass jars and sealing them airtight after heating them in boiling water.

Nicolas Appert, who won the prize offered by the French government, which was looking for a way to preserve food without it spoiling so as to feed its armies on long campaigns, laid the foundations of canning by putting food into glass jars and heating them in boiling water after sealing them airtight.

The French government, which was looking for a way to preserve food without it spoiling so as to feed its armies on long campaigns, laid the foundations of canning by giving its prize to Nicolas Appert, who put food into glass jars and heated them in boiling water after sealing them airtight.

Because Nicolas Appert won the prize offered by the French government, which was looking for a way to preserve food without it spoiling so as to feed its armies on long campaigns, he was able to lay the foundations of canning by putting food into glass jars and heating them in boiling water after sealing them airtight.
s.a: Özne "ödülünü kazanan Nicolas Appert", yüklem "temelini atmıştır" = laid the foundations of. İşlem sırası "kapattıktan sonra kaynar suda ısıtarak". Doğru şık "heating them in boiling water after sealing them airtight". "sealing … after heating" diyen şık sırayı ters çeviriyor; "Because" diyen şık ödülü sebebe dönüştürüyor.

s.q: While volcanic ash can devastate crops in the short term, it breaks down over time into minerals that make the surrounding soil exceptionally fertile.
o: Volkanik kül kısa vadede ekinleri mahvedebilse de zamanla ayrışarak çevredeki toprağı son derece verimli kılan minerallere dönüşür.
Volkanik kül kısa vadede ekinleri mahvedebilse de zamanla ayrışan ekinler, çevredeki toprağı son derece verimli kılan minerallere dönüşür.
Volkanik kül zamanla ekinleri mahvedebilse de kısa vadede ayrışarak çevredeki toprağı son derece verimli kılan minerallere dönüşür.
Volkanik kül, çevredeki toprağı son derece verimli kılmak için zamanla ayrışarak minerallere dönüşse de kısa vadede ekinleri mahvedebilir.
Volkanik kül kısa vadede ekinleri mahvetse de çevredeki toprağı son derece verimli kılan minerallere ancak uzun yıllar sonra dönüşebilir.
s.a: "While" burada zıtlık: mahvedebilse de. Ana yüklem "breaks down … into minerals" (ayrışarak minerallere dönüşür), "that make the soil fertile" mineralleri niteliyor. Doğru şık bu sırayı koruyor. En güçlü çeldirici iki zaman zarfının yerini değiştiriyor; zarar zamanla, ayrışma kısa vadede olmuş.

s.q: It is believed that the first domesticated dogs were descended from a population of wolves that has since become extinct.
o: The first domesticated dogs are believed to be descended from wolves that are still alive today.
It is certain that a now extinct population of wolves was descended from the first domesticated dogs.
The first domesticated dogs are believed to have caused the extinction of the wolves from which they were descended.
It is believed that wolves became extinct shortly after the first dogs were domesticated.
The first domesticated dogs are thought to have descended from a group of wolves that no longer exists.
s.a: Kökte "It is believed that" ve iki bilgi var: ilk köpekler bir kurt topluluğundan geliyor, o topluluk artık yok. "are thought to have descended … no longer exists" ikisini de koruyor. "still alive today" bilgiyi ters çeviriyor; "It is certain" inancı kesinliğe çevirip soy yönünü de tersine kuruyor.

s.q: The rapid spread of mobile phones in parts of Africa has allowed many people to use banking services without ever having opened an account at a traditional bank.
o: Many people in parts of Africa have had to open accounts at traditional banks before they could use mobile phones.
Traditional banks in parts of Africa have encouraged the spread of mobile phones in order to attract new customers.
Thanks to the swift spread of mobile phones in some African regions, numerous people have gained access to banking services without holding a conventional bank account.
The spread of mobile phones in parts of Africa has been slow because most people there do not have bank accounts.
In parts of Africa, mobile phones are mainly used for banking by people who already have accounts at traditional banks.
s.a: Kökte sebep-sonuç var: cep telefonunun hızlı yayılması, banka hesabı olmayanlara bankacılık hizmeti sağladı. "Thanks to the swift spread … without holding a conventional bank account" sebebi ve sonucu koruyor. Hesabı ön şart yapan şık ilişkiyi tersine çeviriyor; bankaları özne yapan şık kökte olmayan bir amaç ekliyor.

s.q: Without the invention of the microscope, scientists might not have discovered bacteria until much later.
o: If the microscope had not been invented, the discovery of bacteria might have been delayed considerably.
Scientists discovered bacteria long before the microscope was invented, although they could not study them in detail.
The microscope was invented so that scientists could find out what caused diseases spread by bacteria.
Even without the microscope, scientists would have discovered bacteria at about the same time.
Bacteria were discovered much later than expected because early microscopes were not powerful enough.
s.a: Kökteki "Without … might not have discovered … until much later" geçmişe dair gerçek dışı bir koşul ve bir ihtimal bildiriyor. Aynı koşulu ve might'ı koruyan şık: If the microscope had not been invented, the discovery of bacteria might have been delayed considerably. "about the same time" diyen şık mikroskobun etkisini yok sayıyor.

s.q: The opening of the new hospital has been delayed because some of the medical equipment has not arrived yet.
o: Some of the medical equipment has been delayed because the new hospital opened earlier than planned.
Since part of the medical equipment is still missing, the new hospital will open later than planned.
The new hospital has opened, although some of its medical equipment has not been delivered yet.
The new hospital will not open at all, as most of its medical equipment has been lost.
The medical equipment for the new hospital arrived late, but the opening took place on time.
s.a: Kökte sebep-sonuç var: ekipmanın bir kısmı gelmedi, bu yüzden açılış gecikti. "Since part of the medical equipment is still missing" sebebi, "will open later than planned" sonucu karşılıyor. "has opened" ve "took place on time" sonucu ters çeviriyor; "not … at all" ile "most" ise kesinliği ve miktarı abartıyor.

s.q: It is unlikely that the global demand for lithium will be met in the coming decade unless new mining projects are approved much more quickly than at present.
o: Unless approval for new mining projects is speeded up considerably, the world will probably not have enough lithium to meet demand over the next ten years.
The global demand for lithium will certainly fall in the coming decade because new mining projects are being approved too slowly.
New mining projects are being approved more quickly than ever, so the global demand for lithium is likely to be met in the coming decade.
Even if new mining projects are approved much more quickly, the global demand for lithium will not be met in the coming decade.
The global demand for lithium has not been met in the past decade because new mining projects were approved too slowly.
s.a: Kökte iki ipucu var: "It is unlikely" (olası değil) ve "unless" ile kurulan şart. "will probably not have enough … Unless … speeded up" ikisini de koruyor. "Even if" şartı kaldırıp sonucu kesinleştiriyor; "will certainly fall" ve geçmişten söz eden şık kesinliği ve zamanı kaydırıyor.

s.q: Children who read regularly for pleasure tend to have a wider vocabulary than those who rarely read.
o: Children who often read for enjoyment generally have a richer vocabulary than those who seldom read.
Children with a wide vocabulary tend to enjoy reading more than those whose vocabulary is limited.
Children who rarely read for pleasure always have a poorer vocabulary than those who read regularly.
Reading for pleasure is the only way for children to widen their vocabulary.
Children who read regularly do so for pleasure rather than to improve their vocabulary.
s.a: Kökte "tend to" (eğilimindedir) ve "wider … than" karşılaştırması var. "generally have a richer vocabulary than those who seldom read" hem eğilimi hem karşılaştırmanın yönünü koruyor. "always" ve "the only way" keskin ifade ekliyor; kelime bilgisini sebep yapan şık ilişkiyi ters kuruyor.

s.q: While the extinction of the dinosaurs is usually attributed to an asteroid impact, some researchers argue that massive volcanic eruptions in what is now India had already weakened many species.
o: Some researchers claim that the asteroid impact which killed the dinosaurs also triggered massive volcanic eruptions in what is now India.
Most researchers now agree that volcanic eruptions in what is now India, rather than an asteroid impact, caused the extinction of the dinosaurs.
Because many species had already been weakened by volcanic eruptions, the asteroid impact had little effect on the dinosaurs.
Although an asteroid impact is generally held responsible for the dinosaurs' extinction, it has been suggested that many species were already in decline due to huge eruptions in present-day India.
Researchers have long debated whether the dinosaurs were weakened by an asteroid impact before massive volcanic eruptions in India finished them off.
s.a: Kökte "While" ile iki görüş var: yaygın açıklama asteroit, bazı araştırmacılara göre ise Hindistan'daki volkanlar türleri zaten zayıflatmıştı. "Although … generally held responsible … it has been suggested" bu dengeyi koruyor. "Most researchers now agree" azınlık görüşünü genel kabule çeviriyor; "little effect" kökte yok.

s.q: The higher a city's population density, the less energy each resident tends to use for transport.
o: Residents of densely populated cities use more energy for transport because they have to travel longer distances.
In cities where more people live close together, residents generally consume less energy getting around.
Cities that use less energy for transport tend to attract more residents than other cities.
Population density has little effect on how much energy residents use for transport.
As cities grow larger, their residents always need more energy for transport.
s.a: Kökteki "The higher …, the less …" kalıbı ters orantı veriyor: yoğunluk arttıkça kişi başı ulaşım enerjisi azalıyor. "more people live close together … consume less energy" bu yönü koruyor, "tends to" da "generally" ile eşleşiyor. "use more energy" yönü ters çeviriyor; nüfusu sonuç yapan şık ilişkiyi tersine kuruyor.

s.q: It was not so much the cost of the project as its likely impact on the environment that led the council to reject it.
o: The council rejected the project because it was considered both far too expensive and equally harmful to the environment.
Although the project would not harm the environment in any way, the council rejected it because of its high cost.
The council rejected the project mainly because of the damage it could cause to the environment rather than its cost.
The council accepted the project despite its high cost, as its impact on the environment was expected to be limited.
The cost of the project was the main reason why the council became so concerned about its impact on the environment.
s.a: Kökteki "not so much X as Y" kalıbı "X'ten çok Y" demek: reddin asıl sebebi maliyet değil çevresel etki. Bunu "mainly because of the damage … rather than its cost" karşılıyor. "both … and equally" iki sebebi eşitliyor; yalnız maliyete bağlayan ve "accepted" diyen şıklar anlamı ters kuruyor.

s.q: No sooner had the new policy been announced than it came under fierce criticism from opposition parties.
o: Opposition parties had fiercely criticised the new policy long before it was officially announced by the government.
The new policy was harshly criticised by opposition parties as soon as it was announced.
It was only some time after the new policy had been announced that opposition parties began to criticise it fiercely.
The government announced the new policy despite the fierce criticism it had already received from opposition parties.
Opposition parties did not criticise the new policy until its effects on the economy had become clear.
s.a: Kökteki "No sooner had … than" "-ir -mez" anlamı veriyor: politika açıklanır açıklanmaz sert eleştiri aldı. "as soon as it was announced" bunu, "harshly" de "fierce" sözcüğünü karşılıyor. "long before", "only some time after" ve "did not … until" şıkları zaman ilişkisini kaydırıyor.

s.q: Most plants need sunlight to grow, but some species that live on the forest floor can survive in deep shade.
o: Species that live on the forest floor need more sunlight than most other plants in order to grow.
Most plants that grow in deep shade on the forest floor eventually die because they lack sunlight.
Since there is little sunlight on the forest floor, no plants are able to survive there.
Some plants on the forest floor grow in deep shade because they are damaged by direct sunlight.
Although sunlight is necessary for the growth of most plants, certain forest-floor species are able to live in very little light.
s.a: Kökte "but" ile zıtlık var: çoğu bitki güneş ister, orman tabanındaki bazı türler ise gölgede yaşayabilir. Cevapta zıtlık "Although" ile geliyor; "some" = "certain", "can survive" = "are able to live". "no plants" keskin bir genelleme; "damaged by direct sunlight" kökte olmayan bir sebep ekliyor.

s.q: Many museums now put images of their collections online, which allows people who are unable to travel to see rare objects.
o: Many museums have started to display rare objects online since people are no longer willing to travel to see them.
People who are unable to travel can only see rare objects if museums put images of them online.
Thanks to the images of their collections that many museums now publish online, people who cannot travel are able to see rare objects.
Although many museums put images of their collections online, rare objects can still be seen only by people who travel.
Many museums are unable to put images of their rare objects online, so people have to travel to see them.
s.a: Kökte sebep-sonuç var: müzeler koleksiyon görsellerini internete koyuyor, bu da seyahat edemeyenlerin nadir eserleri görmesini sağlıyor. "Thanks to … people who cannot travel are able to see" bu ilişkiyi koruyor. "only if" kökte olmayan keskin bir şart ekliyor; "no longer willing to travel" sebep-sonucu ters kuruyor.

s.q: Hardly any of the ancient city's original buildings have survived, as most were destroyed by a series of earthquakes.
o: Most of the ancient city's original buildings have survived, although several earthquakes struck the region.
Very few of the ancient city's original buildings remain today because the majority were ruined by successive earthquakes.
None of the ancient city's original buildings was damaged by the earthquakes that struck it.
The earthquakes that destroyed the ancient city were caused by the weight of its many buildings.
Some of the ancient city's original buildings have survived, but it is not known what destroyed the rest.
s.a: Kökteki "Hardly any" (neredeyse hiç) "very few" ile, "most were destroyed" de "the majority were ruined" ile eşleşiyor; sebep "as" yerine "because" ile geliyor. "Most … have survived" miktarı ters çeviriyor; yıkımın sebebini bilinmez sayan şık kökteki depremleri yok sayıyor.

s.q: No other ocean on Earth is as large or as deep as the Pacific.
o: The Pacific is larger than the other oceans, but some of them are deeper.
The Pacific is neither the largest nor the deepest ocean on Earth.
The other oceans on Earth are as large and as deep as the Pacific.
The Pacific is both the largest and the deepest of all the Earth's oceans.
The Pacific is the deepest ocean on Earth, although it is not the largest.
s.a: Kökteki "No other … as large or as deep as" aslında üstünlük bildiriyor: hiçbir okyanus onun kadar büyük ve derin değil. Kulağı tersten tutuyoruz: Pasifik hem en büyük hem en derin okyanus. Öteki şıklar iki özellikten birini ya da ikisini birden ters çeviriyor ya da eşitliğe dönüştürüyor.

s.q: Contrary to the widely held view that Neanderthals were primitive, recent discoveries suggest that they made jewellery, buried their dead and may even have produced cave art.
o: Recent discoveries confirm the widely held view that Neanderthals were too primitive to produce cave art, although they buried their dead.
Although Neanderthals are commonly regarded as primitive, recent findings indicate that they made ornaments, buried the dead and possibly created cave paintings.
Recent discoveries have proved beyond doubt that Neanderthals produced most of the cave art that was once attributed to modern humans.
The widely held view that Neanderthals were primitive is based on the fact that they made jewellery and buried their dead.
Since Neanderthals made jewellery and buried their dead, many people believe that they also produced cave art.
