s.a: Kökte "Contrary to the widely held view" zıtlığı ve "may even have" olasılığı var. "Although … commonly regarded as primitive, recent findings indicate … possibly created" hem zıtlığı hem olasılığı koruyor. "proved beyond doubt" olasılığı kesinliğe, "confirm" ise zıtlığı onaya çeviriyor.

s.q: The study's findings, however striking, should be interpreted with caution given the small number of participants involved.
o: No matter how remarkable the study's findings may be, they need to be treated carefully, as only a few people took part in it.
Because the study involved a large number of participants from many different countries, its striking findings can safely be trusted.
The study's findings are not particularly striking, since only a very small number of participants were involved in it.
Although the study involved few participants, its findings are striking enough to be accepted without any caution at all.
The small number of participants made it difficult for the researchers to produce any striking findings.
s.a: Kökte iki ipucu var: "however striking" (ne kadar çarpıcı olursa olsun) ve "given the small number of participants" (katılımcı azlığı göz önüne alınınca). "No matter how remarkable" ile "only a few people took part" ikisini de karşılıyor. "large number" diyen şık miktarı, "without any caution" diyen şık yorumu ters çeviriyor.

s.q: Visitors are not allowed to take photographs inside the cave, as the flash can damage the ancient paintings on its walls.
o: Visitors may take photographs inside the cave as long as they do not touch the ancient paintings on its walls.
The ancient paintings on the walls of the cave were damaged because visitors took photographs with a flash.
Taking photographs is forbidden inside the cave because the light from a flash may harm the ancient wall paintings.
Visitors are encouraged to photograph the ancient paintings in the cave so that they can be studied later.
Only visitors with special permission are allowed to use a flash when photographing the paintings in the cave.
s.a: Kökte iki ipucu var: "not allowed" (yasak) ve "as" ile verilen sebep, flaşın resimlere zarar verebilmesi. "forbidden … because … may harm" ikisini de karşılıyor. Resimlerin zarar gördüğünü söyleyen şık olasılığı gerçekleşmiş bir olaya çeviriyor; izinli ziyaretçi şıkkı kökte olmayan bir istisna ekliyor.

s.q: Few inventions have changed daily life as profoundly as electric lighting.
o: Electric lighting has changed daily life more than most inventions.
Electric lighting has changed daily life less than most other inventions.
Daily life has changed so much that electric lighting is no longer considered an important invention.
Only a few people realise how much electric lighting has changed their daily lives.
Many inventions, including electric lighting, have failed to change daily life significantly.
s.a: Kökte miktar ifadesi var: "Few inventions … as profoundly as" (pek az buluş onun kadar derinden değiştirdi). Kulağı tersten tutuyoruz: elektrik aydınlatması günlük hayatı çoğu buluştan daha çok değiştirdi. "less than most" kıyasın yönünü ters çeviriyor; "Only a few people realise" ise miktarı buluştan insana kaydırıyor.

s.q: Had the bridge been inspected more regularly, the structural weaknesses that led to its collapse might have been detected in time.
o: Although the bridge was inspected regularly, its structural weaknesses were not detected before it collapsed.
If the bridge had been inspected more often, the structural problems that caused it to collapse could have been noticed in time.
The bridge collapsed because inspectors detected its structural weaknesses too late, even though they had inspected it very often.
Regular inspections of the bridge revealed structural weaknesses, which were repaired before it could collapse.
If the structural weaknesses of the bridge are detected in time, regular inspections will not be necessary.
s.a: Kökteki "Had the bridge been inspected" devrik bir if cümlesi: If the bridge had been inspected, yani geçmişe dair gerçek dışı koşul. "might have been detected" de "could have been noticed" ile eşleşiyor. Gerçekte köprü sık denetlenmedi; "Although … was inspected regularly" ve onarıldı diyen şıklar bunu tersine çeviriyor.

s.q: Unlike most mammals, which replace their teeth only once, sharks shed and regrow their teeth continuously throughout their lives.
o: Sharks, like most mammals, replace their teeth only once in their lives.
Most mammals regrow their teeth continuously, whereas sharks replace them only once.
Sharks lose their teeth more often than mammals because their teeth are much weaker.
Sharks and most mammals both shed their teeth, but only sharks are able to replace them.
While the teeth of most mammals are replaced just once, sharks keep losing and growing new teeth for their entire lives.
s.a: Kökte "Unlike" ile karşılaştırma var: memeliler dişlerini bir kez yeniler, köpekbalıkları ömür boyu sürekli. "While … just once, sharks keep … for their entire lives" yönü koruyor. Tarafları yer değiştiren şık karşılaştırmayı ters kuruyor; zayıf diş şıkkı kökte olmayan bir sebep ekliyor.

s.q:
Reporter: - Your team has just discovered a new species of frog in the rainforest. How did you find it?
Biologist: - ----
Reporter: - So it was the frog's call that gave it away?
Biologist: - Exactly. Once we had recorded it and compared it with known species, we realised it was something new.
o: Actually, we heard it before we saw it. Its call was unlike anything we had recorded before, so we followed the sound.
We were studying the frogs that live in the streams, and this one turned up among the others.
Local guides told us where to look, as they had seen it many times before.
It was small and brown, which made it almost impossible to see among the fallen leaves.
We noticed its unusual colour while we were photographing insects at night.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "So it was the frog's call that gave it away?" var: "So" bir özet, boşlukta kurbağanın sesi geçmeli. Önce sesini duyup sesi takip ettiklerini söyleyen şık hem "How did you find it?" sorusuna cevap veriyor hem özete bağlanıyor. Rengini ya da rehberleri anlatan şıklar bulma yolunu veriyor ama sesten söz etmiyor.

s.q:
Lecturer: - Did you manage to finish your essay on time?
Student: - ----
Lecturer: - Well, you should have told me earlier. I can give you two more days.
Student: - Thank you, I really appreciate it.
o: Yes, I handed it in on Monday morning, two days before the deadline you set.
Not quite. I was ill for most of last week and fell behind with my work.
Yes, but I'm not sure whether I followed your instructions correctly.
Not yet, but I'm sure I'll finish it before the deadline tonight.
Could I hand it in by email instead of on paper?
s.a: Boşluğun altında "you should have told me earlier. I can give you two more days" var: öğrenci yetiştirememiş ve bunu geç söylemiş olmalı. "Not quite" ile hastalanıp geride kaldığını anlatan şık iki satıra bağlanıyor. Bu akşam bitireceğini söyleyen şık ek süreyi gereksiz kılıyor.

s.q:
Mark: - Our council wants to ban cars from the town centre next year.
Elena: - I know. The shopkeepers on the high street are already collecting signatures against it.
Mark: - ----
Elena: - Really? I would have assumed the opposite. Why would that be?
Mark: - Apparently, people on foot tend to wander into more shops and stay longer than drivers, who park, buy one thing and leave.
o: I can understand their worry. Many of them depend on customers who drive in from the surrounding villages.
That's odd, because several studies have found that shops in car-free areas often see their sales go up rather than down.
The council says the ban will reduce air pollution and make the streets much safer for children.
Some of them have even threatened to move their businesses to the new shopping centre outside town.
Perhaps the council should offer them lower rents during the first year of the ban.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "I would have assumed the opposite. Why would that be?" var: boşlukta esnafın beklentisinin, satışların düşeceğinin tersi söylenmeli. Arabasız bölgelerde satışların arttığını söyleyen şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Esnafın kaygısını haklı bulan şık beklentiyi doğruladığı için "opposite" ile kopuyor.

s.q:
Student: - Excuse me, I'm looking for a book on the history of climate, but the catalogue says it's on loan.
Librarian: - ----
Student: - Two weeks is a long time. I need it for an essay that's due on Friday.
Librarian: - In that case, you could read the electronic version on our website.
o: Yes, it's on the second floor, in the science section.
I'm afraid it can't be borrowed; it must be read in the library.
That's right. It won't be returned for another two weeks, but you can reserve it.
We have several other books on climate history, if you'd like to see them.
Students can borrow up to ten books at a time.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "Two weeks is a long time" var: "Two weeks" ifadesinin karşılığı boşlukta olmalı. Kitabın iki hafta daha dönmeyeceğini söyleyen şık hem "on loan" bilgisini sürdürüyor hem alt satıra bağlanıyor. Başka kitap öneren şık konu içinde ama süreye gönderme yapmıyor.

s.q:
Journalist: - You opened your bookshop just as two others in the town were closing. Weren't you worried?
Owner: - Of course. Everyone told me I could never compete with online sellers on price.
Journalist: - ----
Owner: - Exactly. We hold readings, book clubs and children's story hours almost every evening.
Journalist: - So you see the shop as a meeting place rather than just a place to buy books?
o: Have online sellers really made books that much cheaper than they used to be?
Did you have any experience of running a business before you opened the shop?
So you decided to offer people something a website can't, rather than trying to match its prices?
Do you think the other two shops closed simply because their owners retired?
So you decided to lower your prices to the same level as the big websites?
s.a: Boşluğun altında "Exactly. We hold readings, book clubs …" var: boşlukta etkinliklerle doğrulanacak bir yorum olmalı. Üstte fiyatla rekabet edilemeyeceği söylenmiş. İnternetin veremeyeceği bir şey sunmayı soran şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Fiyatları indirmeyi soran şık üste bağlanıyor ama etkinlik cevabıyla kopuyor.

s.q:
Customer: - I bought this laptop last week, but the battery runs out after just an hour.
Shop assistant: - ----
Customer: - No, I haven't. Should I?
Shop assistant: - Yes, sometimes an update fixes battery problems. If it doesn't, we'll replace it.
o: This model's battery usually lasts about eight hours, so it shouldn't run out so quickly.
Batteries often wear out faster if the laptop is left plugged in all the time.
I'm sorry to hear that. Have you installed the latest update?
Have you kept the receipt? We can't replace it without proof of purchase.
Did you buy it from this shop or from our website?
s.a: Boşluğun altında "No, I haven't. Should I?" var: boşlukta "Have you …?" ile kurulan bir soru olmalı. Fiş soran şık da bu kalıba uyuyor ama son satır güncellemeden söz ediyor; "Have you installed the latest update?" iki satıra birden bağlanıyor. Pilin ömrünü anlatan şıklar soru içermiyor.

s.q:
Chloe: - Have you finished the reading for tomorrow's seminar?
Ryan: - Almost. I've still got the last chapter to go.
Chloe: - ----
Ryan: - Is it? In that case, I'd better read it tonight rather than on the bus tomorrow.
o: I've read it twice already.
The seminar has been moved to the large hall.
Do you think the lecturer will ask us questions about it?
Make sure you read it carefully. It's the part the whole discussion will focus on.
I found the first chapter the most interesting.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "Is it?" var: boşlukta "it is" ile kurulan ve son bölümü önemli kılan bir cümle olmalı. Tartışmanın o bölüme odaklanacağını söyleyen şık hem "Is it?" tepkisini hem bu gece okuma kararını açıklıyor. Salonun değiştiğini söyleyen şık "Has it?" isterdi.

s.q:
Ali: - I'm thinking of applying for a job abroad, but I'm not sure.
Elif: - ----
Ali: - You're right. I'd probably regret it if I didn't at least try.
Elif: - Exactly. You can always come back if it doesn't work out.
o: Have you talked to anyone who has worked abroad? They might help you decide.
Why not? It would be a great experience, even if it's only for a year or two.
Jobs abroad usually pay much less than jobs here.
It's a big decision. Perhaps you should wait until you feel more certain.
You should finish your degree first and then start applying for jobs.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "You're right. I'd probably regret it if I didn't at least try" var: boşlukta onu denemeye teşvik eden bir görüş olmalı. "Why not? It would be a great experience" bu desteği veriyor. Beklemeyi öneren ya da düşük maaşa dikkat çeken şıklar "try" kararıyla çelişiyor.

s.q:
Hannah: - My nephew told me the Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure you can see from space.
Owen: - I've heard that a lot, but I've also read that it's a myth.
Hannah: - A myth? But it's thousands of kilometres long!
Owen: - ----
Hannah: - So length alone doesn't make something visible from orbit, then?
Owen: - Exactly. Motorways and airports are often easier to spot, because they contrast more sharply with the land around them.
o: That's true, and some parts of it are wide enough for several horses to ride side by side along the top.
Length isn't the problem; width is. It's just a few metres wide and blends into the land around it.
It was built over many centuries by different dynasties, so some sections are much older than others.
You're right, and on a clear day astronauts say it can apparently be seen even from the Moon.
Most of the sections that tourists visit today were rebuilt in stone and brick several centuries ago.
s.a: Üstte "But it's thousands of kilometres long!" itirazı, altta "So length alone doesn't make something visible" özeti var: boşlukta sorunun uzunluk değil başka bir özellik olduğu söylenmeli. "Length isn't the problem; width is" diyen şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Ay'dan görülebildiğini söyleyen şık özetle çelişiyor.

s.q:
Patient: - I've been sleeping badly for weeks, so I was going to ask you for some sleeping pills.
Doctor: - Before we talk about pills, tell me a little about your evenings. What do you usually do before bed?
Patient: - I often answer work emails in bed, and I usually have a coffee after dinner to stay alert.
Doctor: - ----
Patient: - So you think changing those habits might work better than medication?
o: Coffee in the evening is a common habit, and many patients tell me they actually find it relaxing rather than stimulating.
In that case, a mild sleeping pill for a few nights should be enough to break the pattern.
How long have you been in a job that requires you to answer emails so late in the evening?
Both of those could easily be keeping you awake. Screens and caffeine late in the day are two of the most common causes of poor sleep.
Sleeping pills are generally safe for short periods, as long as you take them exactly as prescribed.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "So you think changing those habits might work better than medication?" var: boşlukta hastanın anlattığı alışkanlıkların uykusuzluğa yol açtığı söylenmeli. Ekran ve kafeini en yaygın sebepler arasında sayan şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Hafif uyku ilacı öneren şık "better than medication" ile çelişiyor.

s.q:
Researcher: - Our survey of three thousand employees shows that people who cycle to work report higher job satisfaction than those who drive.
Colleague: - Interesting. Did you find the same pattern in every sector?
Researcher: - More or less, though the gap was largest in finance and technology.
Colleague: - ----
Researcher: - That's a fair point. We'll need to control for income and job type in the next study.
Colleague: - Otherwise it'll be hard to claim that cycling itself is the cause.
o: That makes sense, since cycling is an excellent way of reducing stress before a long working day.
Did you also ask how far each participant lived from their office?
How many of the participants in those two sectors were women?
Couldn't that be because people in well-paid, flexible jobs are simply more likely to cycle in the first place?
According to several other surveys, job satisfaction in finance has been falling for years.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "That's a fair point. We'll need to control for income and job type" var: boşlukta gelire ve iş türüne dayanan bir itiraz olmalı. İyi ücretli, esnek işi olanların zaten bisiklete binebileceğini soran şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Ev ile iş arası mesafeyi soran şık konu içinde ama gelire ve iş türüne bağlanmıyor.

s.q:
Mia: - I've started drinking a glass of water as soon as I wake up. Someone told me it helps.
Tom: - Helps with what, exactly? Your body has been without water all night, so I suppose it makes sense.
Mia: - ----
Tom: - Well, I'm not sure about that. You'd probably have to change your diet as well before you noticed any difference in your weight.
o: Yes, I've been doing it every morning for about a month now.
Not much, honestly; I usually have a cup of coffee instead.
I read somewhere that water is better for you than fruit juice.
Apparently, it wakes up your brain and improves your memory for the whole day.
Mainly with losing weight. Apparently, it makes you feel less hungry at breakfast.
s.a: Boşluk hem üste hem alta bağlanmalı. Üstte "Helps with what, exactly?" sorusu, altta ise kiloya dair bir şüphe var. Amacını kilo vermek olarak açıklayan "Mainly with losing weight" iki satıra da bağlanıyor. Belleği güçlendirdiğini söyleyen şık soruya cevap veriyor ama alttaki kilo yorumuyla kopuyor.

s.q:
Interviewer: - Your company switched to a four-day working week last year. Was it difficult to persuade the board?
Manager: - Very. Most of them were convinced that we would lose a day's worth of work every week.
Interviewer: - ----
Manager: - On the contrary, it has stayed the same, and in some departments it has actually risen.
Interviewer: - That's surprising. How do you explain it?
Manager: - People are less tired, so they waste less time and make fewer mistakes.
o: And were they right? Has the company's output fallen since the change?
How did you finally manage to change their minds?
Did your employees ask for the change, or was it the management's own idea?
Have any other companies in your sector followed your example since then?
Which departments were the most enthusiastic about trying it?
s.a: Boşluğun altında "On the contrary, it has stayed the same" var: boşlukta bir düşüşü varsayan soru olmalı, it de onun karşılığı. Üstte yönetimin iş kaybı beklentisi var. "Has the company's output fallen since the change?" iki yana bağlanıyor. Yönetimin nasıl ikna edildiğini soran şık "On the contrary" ile cevaplanmıyor.

s.q:
Journalist: - Your latest study suggests that people greatly overestimate how much others notice their mistakes.
Psychologist: - That's right. Participants who made an obvious error in front of a group expected about half of the group to remember it, but only around a quarter actually did.
Journalist: - ----
Psychologist: - Largely because we're so focused on our own behaviour that we find it hard to imagine others aren't.
Journalist: - So everyone else is too busy worrying about themselves to pay much attention to us?
o: Did the participants know in advance that they would be asked to make a mistake in public?
Were the people who made mistakes still feeling embarrassed when you spoke to them later?
How many people took part in the study altogether, and how were they selected?
Isn't it true that some cultures are far less tolerant of public mistakes than others?
That's quite a gap. Why do you think we misjudge other people's attention so badly?
s.a: Boşluğun altında "Largely because …" var: because ile gelen cevap, boşlukta bir why sorusu ister. Üstte beklenti ile gerçek arasındaki fark verilmiş. "That's quite a gap" diyerek bu farkın sebebini soran şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Katılımcı sayısını ya da kültür farkını soran şıklar konu içinde ama because cevabını karşılamıyor.

s.q:
Sophie: - I'm going hiking in the mountains next weekend. Do you think I should take a water filter?
Daniel: - Definitely. Even the clearest mountain streams can contain bacteria.
Sophie: - But I'll be carrying enough water for the whole day anyway.
Daniel: - ----
Sophie: - Good point. I hadn't thought about the weather changing.
o: Then you probably won't need it, as long as you don't drink from the streams.
Most hikers prefer bottled water because it tastes better than stream water.
Bacteria in mountain streams are usually harmless to healthy adults.
What if a storm keeps you out much longer than you planned, though?
Filters are quite expensive, so you could borrow mine if you like.
s.a: Boşluğun altında "Good point. I hadn't thought about the weather changing" var: boşlukta havanın bozulabileceğine dair bir uyarı olmalı. Daniel filtreyi savunuyor; fırtınada uzun kalma ihtimalini soran şık bu tutumu sürdürüyor. Filtreye gerek olmadığını söyleyen şık hem tutumu tersine çeviriyor hem havadan söz etmiyor.

s.q:
Doctor: - How long have you been having these headaches?
Patient: - ----
Doctor: - I see. Have you changed anything in your routine recently, such as your working hours?
Patient: - Actually, yes. I've been spending much longer in front of a computer screen.
o: Usually when I've been staring at a screen for a long time.
They seem to get worse whenever I skip breakfast.
I usually take a painkiller, but it doesn't help much any more.
Only on weekdays, never at the weekend.
For about three weeks now, mostly in the late afternoon.
s.a: Doktor "How long" diye soruyor: boşlukta süre bildiren bir cevap olmalı. "For about three weeks now" süreyi veriyor ve doktorun son dönemdeki değişiklikleri sormasına zemin hazırlıyor. Ekran şıkkı süre vermiyor; üstelik hasta ekran bilgisini ancak son satırda yeni bir bilgi olarak söylüyor.

s.q:
Student: - I don't understand why the Romans abandoned some of their provinces.
Historian: - ----
Student: - So holding on to them simply cost more than they were worth?
Historian: - In many cases, yes, especially when the empire was under pressure elsewhere.
o: The Romans built thousands of kilometres of roads across their territory to move their armies quickly.
Latin remained the language of education in Europe for centuries.
Some provinces were famous for their wine and olive oil.
Defending distant borders took more soldiers and money than the empire could often afford.
Historians still disagree about the exact date when the empire began.
s.a: Soru bazı eyaletlerin neden terk edildiği; boşluğun altında "So holding on to them simply cost more than they were worth?" özeti var. Boşlukta bir maliyet sebebi olmalı. Uzak sınırları savunmanın karşılanamayacak kadar asker ve para gerektirdiğini söyleyen şık özete bağlanıyor. Yollar ve şarap şıkları cevap değil.

s.q:
Paul: - I've been trying to grow tomatoes on my balcony, but the plants are tall and thin, and there's hardly any fruit.
Nora: - Which direction does your balcony face?
Paul: - ----
Nora: - That explains it, then. Tomatoes need at least six hours of direct sunlight a day.
o: North, so it only gets the sun early in the morning.
I water them every evening, sometimes twice a day.
It faces the street, so it's quite noisy.
I bought the seeds from a garden centre near my office.
South, and the plants are in the sun from morning till evening.
s.a: Boşluk hem üstteki "Which direction …?" sorusuna cevap olmalı hem alttaki "That explains it" ile sorunu açıklamalı. Altta güneş ışığı ihtiyacı söyleniyor; balkonun kuzeye baktığını ve az güneş aldığını söyleyen şık iki satıra bağlanıyor. Güneye bakan şık soruya cevap veriyor ama sorunu açıklamıyor.

s.q:
Interviewer: - Many people assume that creativity declines with age. Is there any truth in that?
Psychologist: - It depends on what you measure. In tests where people must produce as many ideas as possible in a few minutes, younger adults usually do better.
Interviewer: - ----
Psychologist: - Not at all. When experts rate the quality of those ideas, older participants often come out ahead.
Interviewer: - So older people may produce fewer ideas, but better ones?
o: So you'd agree that the common view is basically right, then?
Why do younger adults find it so much easier to think quickly under time pressure?
Do the same tests work equally well with young children?
How long do participants usually have to complete these tests?
What kinds of ideas are people usually asked to come up with in these tests?
s.a: Boşluğun altında "Not at all" ve ardından niteliğe göre yaşlıların öne geçtiği var: boşlukta yaygın görüşü doğrulayan bir evet-hayır sorusu olmalı. Üstte gençlerin hızda önde olduğu söylenmiş. "the common view is basically right" diyen şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Gençlerin hızının sebebini soran şık "Not at all" ile cevaplanmıyor.

s.q:
Interviewer: - You've just published your twelfth novel. Congratulations!
Author: - Thank you. It took me nearly four years, which is longer than any of the others.
Interviewer: - Really? I'd have thought writing would get easier with experience.
Author: - ----
Interviewer: - That sounds exhausting. How do you keep going?
Author: - I remind myself that every book I've finished once felt impossible too.
o: It does, in a way. I now plan every chapter in detail before I start, so I rarely get stuck.
My readers seem to prefer my earlier novels, which were much shorter and lighter in tone.
If anything, it's the opposite. Each new book seems to demand that I learn how to write all over again.
I usually write in the mornings and spend the afternoons reading and answering letters from readers.
Several readers have asked me for a sequel, so I've already started planning the next book.
s.a: Üstte "I'd have thought writing would get easier" beklentisi, altta "That sounds exhausting" tepkisi var: boşlukta beklentinin tersi, yazmanın zorlaştığı söylenmeli. "If anything, it's the opposite" diyen şık iki yana bağlanıyor. Bölümleri planlayıp takılmadığını söyleyen şık beklentiyi doğruluyor.

s.q: (I) Most central banks in developed economies try to keep inflation close to two per cent a year, chiefly by raising or lowering interest rates. (II) Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money, but this loss is not shared equally. (III) People on fixed incomes, such as pensioners, tend to bear the heaviest burden, as their incomes do not rise with prices. (IV) Borrowers, by contrast, may benefit, since the real value of their debts falls over time. (V) Savers who keep their money in accounts with low interest rates also see the real value of their savings decline.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: Konu ve limit II'de: enflasyonun yarattığı kayıp herkese eşit dağılmıyor. III sabit gelirlileri, IV "by contrast" ile borçluları, V "also" ile tasarruf sahiplerini sıralıyor. I merkez bankalarının enflasyon hedefini anlatıyor; konu aynı ama "kim nasıl etkileniyor" limitinin dışında. V'teki faiz sözcüğü tuzak.

s.q: (I) Dogs were probably the first animals to be domesticated by humans. (II) Early hunters may have found that wolves which stayed near their camps were useful for hunting and protection. (III) Over thousands of generations, these animals gradually became tamer and more dependent on people. (IV) Some dogs, such as the greyhound, can run at more than sixty kilometres an hour. (V) Today, there are hundreds of dog breeds, each developed for a particular purpose.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu köpeğin evcilleştirilmesi. II kurtların kamplara yaklaşmasını, III "these animals" ile evcilleşmeyi, V bugünkü ırkları veriyor. IV tazının hızına geçiyor; kahraman aynı ama evcilleşme süreci limitinin dışında. Çıkarınca III ile V kronolojik olarak bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Many migratory birds travel thousands of kilometres between their breeding and wintering grounds every year. (II) Remarkably, they often return to exactly the same nesting site. (III) Scientists believe that they find their way by combining several cues, including the position of the sun and the stars. (IV) Some species also appear to be able to sense the Earth's magnetic field and use it as a kind of compass. (V) The Arctic tern, one of these long-distance travellers, can live for more than thirty years.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu göçmen kuşlar; II'den itibaren limit, aynı yuvaya nasıl geri döndükleri. III ve IV güneş, yıldızlar ve manyetik alan gibi yön bulma ipuçlarını veriyor. V kutup sumrusunun ömrüne geçiyor; "one of these long-distance travellers" referansı tutsa da yön bulma limitinin dışında.

s.q: (I) City planners often select street trees for their tolerance of pollution, compacted soil and the limited space available for roots. (II) Trees planted along city streets can lower local temperatures by several degrees in summer. (III) This cooling effect comes mainly from their leaves, which provide shade and release water vapour into the surrounding air. (IV) As a result, neighbourhoods with plenty of trees tend to be noticeably cooler than those with few. (V) For this reason, many city councils now regard tree planting as a cheap way of protecting residents from heatwaves.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: Konu ve limit II'de: sokak ağaçlarının kenti serinletmesi. III "This cooling effect" ile nasıl serinlettiğini, IV "As a result" ile sonucu, V "For this reason" ile önlemi veriyor. I ağaç türlerinin hangi ölçütle seçildiğini anlatıyor; konu aynı ama serinletme limitine bağlanmıyor.

s.q: (I) The printing press, developed by Johannes Gutenberg around 1450, made it possible to produce books in large numbers for the first time. (II) Before this, every copy of a book had to be written out by hand, which took months. (III) Within fifty years, millions of books had been printed across Europe. (IV) The resulting spread of ideas played a major part in the religious and scientific changes of the following centuries. (V) Gutenberg himself made little money from his invention, having lost control of his workshop in a legal dispute.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu matbaa, limit kitapların çok sayıda basılabilmesi ve bunun etkileri. II öncesini, III hızlı yayılışı, IV "The resulting spread of ideas" ile sonucu veriyor. V mucidin icadından para kazanamamasına geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama etki limitini tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) The introduction of the standard shipping container in the second half of the twentieth century transformed world trade. (II) Before containers, goods were loaded and unloaded by hand, a slow process that could keep a ship in port for days. (III) Because containers could be moved directly from ships to trains and lorries, loading times and costs fell dramatically. (IV) Container ships are now so large that some of them cannot pass through older canals. (V) Cheaper transport, in turn, made it profitable for companies to manufacture goods in one country and sell them on the other side of the world.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu konteyner, limit dünya ticaretine etkisi. II öncesini, III maliyetin düşüşünü, V "Cheaper transport, in turn" ile bunun üretime etkisini veriyor. IV bugünkü gemilerin büyüklüğüne geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor. Çıkarınca III'teki düşen maliyet V'e doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Clinical trials of new drugs are usually divided into several phases, each designed to answer different questions. (II) In the first phase, a small number of healthy volunteers receive the drug so that its safety can be assessed. (III) Volunteers in some countries are paid for their time, while in others they receive only their travel expenses. (IV) Later phases involve hundreds or thousands of patients and compare the new drug with existing treatments. (V) Only if a drug passes all of these stages can it be approved for general use.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu klinik denemeler, limit evreleri. II ilk evreyi, IV "Later phases" ile sonraki evreleri, V "all of these stages" ile onay şartını veriyor. III gönüllülere yapılan ödemeye geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor. Çıkarınca II ile IV doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight. (II) Most species hunt at night, finding their way in the dark by means of echolocation. (III) They emit high-pitched sounds and listen for the echoes that bounce back from objects around them. (IV) Some bats, however, feed on fruit and rely mainly on their eyesight and sense of smell. (V) This allows bats to detect an insect as small as a mosquito while flying at full speed.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu yarasalar; II ve III limitin yankıyla yön bulma olduğunu gösteriyor. IV meyveyle beslenip göze ve kokuya güvenen yarasalara geçiyor; kahraman aynı ama limit dışı. Çıkarınca V'teki "This allows bats" III'teki yankı sistemine bağlanıp sivrisineği yakalamayı açıklıyor.

s.q: (I) The Amazon rainforest is the largest tropical rainforest in the world. (II) It covers parts of nine countries in South America. (III) Many people living in the region earn their living by fishing in its rivers. (IV) The forest is home to an enormous variety of plants and animals, many of which have not yet been studied. (V) It also plays an important role in regulating the climate of the whole planet.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu Amazon yağmur ormanı; II yerini, IV canlı çeşitliliğini, V iklimdeki rolünü vererek ormanın özelliklerini sıralıyor. III bölge halkının balıkçılıkla geçinmesine geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor. Çıkarınca IV'teki "The forest" II'deki ormana doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Female sea turtles return to the beaches where they hatched in order to lay their own eggs. (II) After digging a hole in the sand at night, a female lays about a hundred eggs and covers them carefully. (III) The temperature of the sand then decides whether the young turtles will be male or female. (IV) When they hatch about two months later, the young turtles head straight for the sea, guided by the brighter light of the horizon. (V) Adult sea turtles can hold their breath for several hours while they rest underwater.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu deniz kaplumbağaları, limit yumurtlama ve yavruların doğuşu. II yumurtlamayı, III cinsiyeti belirleyen sıcaklığı, IV yavruların denize ulaşmasını sırayla veriyor. V yetişkinlerin su altında nefes tutmasına geçiyor; kahraman aynı ama üreme limitinin dışında.

s.q: (I) Volcanic eruptions are not all alike: some release slow rivers of lava, while others are violent explosions. (II) What decides the style of an eruption is mainly the amount of silica in the magma. (III) Magma that is low in silica is runny, so the gases dissolved in it escape easily and the lava flows out quietly. (IV) Magma rich in silica, by contrast, is thick and sticky, and it traps the gases until the pressure becomes great enough to blow the volcano apart. (V) Over time, the ash that falls on the surrounding land produces some of the most fertile soils in the world.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu püskürmelerin farklılığı: sakin lav akıntısı mı, patlama mı. II bunu belirleyenin silika olduğunu, III ve IV "by contrast" ile az ve çok silikalı magmayı karşılaştırıyor. V külün toprağı verimli kılmasına geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama "püskürme türünü ne belirler" limitini tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) The Silk Road was not a single route but a network of trade paths connecting China with the Mediterranean. (II) Along these routes, merchants exchanged goods such as silk, spices and precious metals. (III) Silk is produced by the larvae of moths that feed on mulberry leaves. (IV) Equally important, however, was the exchange of ideas, religions and technologies that travelled with the traders. (V) Buddhism, for example, spread from India to China partly through contacts made along these routes.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu İpek Yolu, limit ise ticaret ağı olarak işlevi: mal ve fikir alışverişi. III konu içinde ama ipeğin nasıl üretildiğini anlatarak limitin dışına çıkıyor. Çıkarınca II'deki mal alışverişi, IV'teki "Equally important, however" ile fikir alışverişine doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) Recycling paper saves trees, water and energy. (II) Each tonne of recycled paper saves a significant amount of water compared with making new paper. (III) Paper made from recycled fibres is often slightly greyer than paper made from new wood pulp. (IV) However, paper fibres become shorter every time they are recycled, so paper cannot be recycled forever. (V) For this reason, new fibres must regularly be added to keep the quality of the paper high.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu kâğıt geri dönüşümü; II faydasını, IV "However" ile sınırını, V "For this reason" ile önlemi veriyor. III geri dönüştürülmüş kâğıdın rengine geçip eksi bir bilgi getiriyor; ardından gelen "However" artıdan eksiye geçişi kuramıyor. Çıkarınca II'deki artı IV'teki "However" ile doğrudan bağlanıyor.

s.q: (I) When people face a threat, the body releases hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol. (II) These hormones increase the heart rate and supply the muscles with extra energy. (III) This reaction, often called the fight-or-flight response, helped our ancestors to escape from danger. (IV) However, when stress continues for long periods, the same hormones can begin to damage health. (V) Cortisol levels are normally highest in the early morning and fall gradually during the day.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu tehdit anında salgılanan hormonlar. II "These hormones" ile etkilerini, III "This reaction" ile savaş ya da kaç tepkisini, IV "However" ile uzun süreli stresin zararını veriyor. V kortizolün gün içindeki doğal değişimine geçiyor; hormon ortak ama stres tepkisi limitinin dışında.

s.q: (I) Physiotherapy helps patients recover movement and strength after an injury, an illness or surgery. (II) Treatment often includes exercises designed to strengthen specific muscles and improve flexibility. (III) Some minor injuries, however, heal completely without any treatment at all. (IV) Physiotherapists may also use techniques such as massage and heat therapy to reduce pain. (V) Patients are usually asked to continue their exercises at home between sessions.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu fizyoterapi, limit hastaların iyileşmesine nasıl yardım ettiği. II egzersizleri, IV "also" ile masaj ve ısı tedavisini, V evde süren egzersizleri veriyor. III bazı yaralanmaların tedavisiz iyileştiğini söyleyip yöntemlerin sıralandığı akışı kesiyor. Çıkarınca IV'teki "also" II'deki egzersizlere eklenebiliyor.

s.q: (I) Most reef-building corals live in partnership with microscopic algae that supply them with food produced through photosynthesis. (II) Coral reefs cover only a tiny fraction of the ocean floor. (III) Nevertheless, they are home to around a quarter of all known marine species. (IV) Reefs also protect coastlines from waves and storms, and they support fishing industries worth billions of dollars. (V) For these reasons, their decline is a matter of serious concern.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: II'den itibaren limit resiflerin önemi: III "Nevertheless" ile küçük alana rağmen tür zenginliği, IV "also" ile kıyıya ve balıkçılığa katkı, V "For these reasons" ile sonuç. I mercanların alglerle ortak yaşamını, yani biyolojisini anlatıyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) The domestication of the horse transformed human societies across the Eurasian steppe. (II) Wild horses had roamed the grasslands of North America long before they disappeared from the continent around 10,000 years ago. (III) Mounted riders could travel and trade over far greater distances than people on foot. (IV) Horses also changed the nature of warfare, giving a decisive advantage to groups that mastered riding. (V) Some historians even link the spread of certain language families to the movements of these horse-riding peoples.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu atın evcilleştirilmesi, limit Avrasya bozkırındaki toplumlara etkisi. III, IV ve V bu etkiyi sıralıyor: ulaşım ve ticaret, savaş, dillerin yayılışı. II Kuzey Amerika'daki yabani atlara geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor: hem yer hem dönem farklı.

s.q: (I) Bilingual children sometimes mix words from their two languages in the same sentence. (II) Parents occasionally worry that this is a sign of confusion. (III) Research suggests, however, that such mixing usually follows grammatical rules and reflects skill rather than difficulty. (IV) Adults who learn a second language often find pronunciation the hardest part. (V) In fact, bilingual adults also switch between languages in conversation, often to express a particular shade of meaning.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu iki dilli çocukların dilleri karıştırması. II ailelerin kaygısını, III "however" ile bunun beceri olduğunu, V "In fact … also" ile iki dilli yetişkinlerin de dil değiştirdiğini veriyor. IV ikinci dil öğrenen yetişkinlerin telaffuz güçlüğüne geçiyor; konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor.

s.q: (I) Iron is an essential mineral that the body needs in order to produce haemoglobin. (II) Haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body. (III) When iron levels are low, people may feel tired and weak and find it hard to concentrate. (IV) In industry, iron is mostly used to make steel, which is far stronger and more durable than the pure metal. (V) To prevent this, doctors usually advise people to eat more iron-rich foods such as red meat, beans and dark green leafy vegetables.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: Konu demirin vücuttaki rolü ve eksikliği. V'teki "To prevent this" III'teki eksikliğe bağlanıyor. IV aynı kelimeyle sanayideki metal demire geçiyor; vücut-sağlık limitinin dışına çıkıp III ile V arasındaki bağı koparıyor. Çıkarınca "this" doğrudan düşük demir düzeyini gösteriyor.

s.q: (I) Groundwater stored in underground aquifers supplies drinking water to roughly half of the world's population. (II) The taste of bottled mineral water depends largely on the minerals it picks up as it passes through different types of rock. (III) In many agricultural regions, however, it is being pumped out far faster than rainfall can replenish it. (IV) As a result, wells must be drilled ever deeper, and in some places the land above the depleted aquifers has begun to sink. (V) Since such damage may take centuries to reverse, hydrologists argue that groundwater should be managed as a finite shared resource rather than an inexhaustible one.
o: I
II
III
IV
V
s.a: İlk cümleden konu yeraltı suyu, limit içme suyu kaynağı olarak önemi; ardından aşırı çekilmesi ve sonuçları geliyor. Maden suyunun tadına geçen II konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor. II çıkınca III'teki "it" I'deki yeraltı suyuna gidiyor ve "however" artıyı doğrudan eksiye çeviriyor.

s.q: Hearing loss is often regarded as an inevitable part of ageing. ---- Exposure to loud noise, whether at work or through personal music players, is a major cause of hearing damage that could be avoided. Protecting the ears from loud sounds is therefore important at every stage of life, not only in old age.
o: Indeed, almost everyone over eighty has some difficulty in hearing.
Hearing aids, as a result, have become much cheaper in recent years.
Children's hearing, for example, is usually tested soon after birth.
However, a significant proportion of cases are in fact preventable.
It is also linked to a higher risk of memory problems in later life.
s.a: İlk cümle yaygın görüşü veriyor: işitme kaybı yaşlanmanın kaçınılmaz parçası. Boşluktan sonra önlenebilir bir sebep, gürültü anlatılıyor; bu geçiş zıtlık ister. "However" ile vakaların önemli kısmının önlenebilir olduğunu söyleyen şık köprüyü kuruyor. "Indeed" ile kanıyı destekleyen şık sonraki cümleye zıt düşüyor.

s.q: Dental decay is one of the most common health problems in the world, affecting both children and adults. ---- These bacteria feed on sugar and produce acids that gradually dissolve the hard outer layer of the teeth. Reducing the amount of sugar in the diet and brushing regularly with fluoride toothpaste can therefore prevent much of the damage.
o: It can, however, be prevented in most cases by simple measures.
Children, for example, often eat more sweets than adults.
This is why most toothpastes now contain fluoride.
Sugary drinks, moreover, are a major source of sugar in many children's diets.
It is caused mainly by bacteria that live in a sticky film on the surface of the teeth.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "These bacteria" var; boşlukta bakteriler geçmeli. Diş çürüğünün "mainly by bacteria" kaynaklandığını söyleyen şık referansı karşılıyor, "It" de ilk cümledeki çürüğe gidiyor. Şekerli içecekleri moreover ile ekleyen şık konu içinde ama bakteriden söz etmediği için referans boşta kalıyor.

s.q: Fermentation is one of the oldest methods of preserving food. ---- These microorganisms convert sugars into acids or alcohol, creating an environment in which harmful bacteria cannot easily survive. As a result, foods such as yoghurt, sauerkraut and kimchi can be stored for much longer than the fresh ingredients from which they are made. In recent years, fermented foods have also attracted attention for their possible effects on gut health.
o: Refrigeration, however, has made this method far less necessary in most homes.
Kimchi, for example, is made mainly from cabbage, radishes and spices.
Like salting and drying, it works by killing the microorganisms that would otherwise spoil the food.
It relies on bacteria and yeasts, which break down the food under controlled conditions.
The process was probably discovered by accident, when stored fruit or milk began to change.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "These microorganisms" var; boşlukta mikroorganizmalar geçmeli ve iş gören taraf olmalı. "It relies on bacteria and yeasts" bunu karşılıyor. Mikroorganizmaları öldürdüğünü söyleyen şık referansa dokunuyor, ama öldürülen canlılar şekeri dönüştüremez; akış çelişiyor.

s.q: Tea was first drunk in China thousands of years ago, possibly as a medicine. ---- From there, it spread along trade routes to Japan, Central Asia and eventually Europe. By the eighteenth century, it had become so popular in Britain that it was being imported in huge quantities, and the government earned a great deal of money by taxing it.
o: Over time, it became an everyday drink enjoyed throughout the country.
Coffee, by contrast, originated in the highlands of Ethiopia.
Its leaves were later exported to Britain in huge quantities.
For this reason, it is still sold mainly in pharmacies in China today.
The British, therefore, began to grow it in their colonies in India.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "From there" var; çayın yayılmaya başladığı yer Çin. Boşluk Çin'de kalmalı ve kronolojiyi sürdürmeli: ilaç olarak başlayan çayın zamanla günlük içecek olduğunu söyleyen şık bunu yapıyor. İngiltere'ye ihracatı ve sömürgelerde yetiştirilmesini anlatan şıklar sonraki yüzyılları öne alıp kronolojiyi bozuyor.

s.q: Many people assume that deserts are lifeless places. ---- Cacti store water in their thick stems, and many desert animals are active only at night, when temperatures are lower. Some species of beetle even collect drinking water from fog by tilting their bodies into the wind. These adaptations show how life can thrive under conditions that seem extremely harsh.
o: Deserts, after all, receive less than 250 millimetres of rain in a typical year.
In fact, many plants and animals have adapted to survive on very little water.
However, most desert animals survive by migrating to wetter areas in summer.
Indeed, very few species can tolerate such extreme heat for long.
Deserts cover about a third of the Earth's land surface, and many of them are expanding.
s.a: İlk cümle yaygın bir kanıyı veriyor: çöller cansız. Boşluktan sonra kaktüs, gece hayvanları ve sisten su toplayan böcek örnekleri geliyor; boşluk kanıyı düzelten genel cümle olmalı. "In fact" ile canlıların az suya uyum sağladığını söyleyen şık oturuyor. "Indeed, very few species" kanıyı destekleyerek yorumu ters kuruyor.

s.q: In the nineteenth century, many doctors did not wash their hands between examining patients. When the Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that women cared for by doctors were dying of fever at a much higher rate than those cared for by midwives, he suspected that doctors were carrying something harmful from the autopsy room. ---- Despite this dramatic result, many of his colleagues rejected his ideas, partly because they did not like being told that they were responsible for their patients' deaths.
o: Midwives in the nineteenth century were often poorly paid and received little formal training.
Today, hand hygiene is considered one of the most important ways of preventing infection in hospitals.
He therefore required doctors in his clinic to wash their hands in a chlorine solution, and the death rate fell sharply.
Semmelweis was born in Buda in 1818 and studied medicine in Vienna.
Some of his colleagues believed that fever was caused by bad air rather than by contact.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "Despite this dramatic result" var: boşlukta çarpıcı bir sonuç olmalı. Doktorun kuşkusundan sonra "therefore" ile klorlu suyla el yıkamayı zorunlu kılan ve ölümlerin hızla düştüğünü söyleyen şık bu sonucu veriyor. Kötü hava görüşü ya da ebelerin ücreti bir sonuç değil.

s.q: Lightning is one of the most powerful forces in nature. A single flash can heat the air around it to a temperature five times hotter than the surface of the Sun. ---- This sudden expansion produces the loud noise that we hear as thunder. Because light travels much faster than sound, we always see the flash before we hear the sound.
o: This is why lightning usually strikes the tallest objects in an area.
As a result, the air glows with the bright light that we see as the flash.
The flash itself lasts for only a fraction of a second.
The heated air expands violently in a fraction of a second.
The air then cools down slowly over several minutes.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "This sudden expansion" var; referansın karşılığı boşlukta ani bir genleşme olmalı. Havanın aşırı ısındığını söyleyen cümleden sonra "The heated air expands violently" genleşmeyi veriyor. Havanın yavaşça soğuduğunu söyleyen şık "sudden" ile çelişiyor; ışığı anlatan şık genleşmeden söz etmiyor.

s.q: Nuclear power stations produce electricity without emitting carbon dioxide, which makes them attractive in the fight against climate change. ---- The waste remains dangerous for thousands of years, and finding a safe place to store it permanently has proved extremely difficult. The cost and time needed to build new reactors have also risen sharply in recent decades.
o: As a result, many countries have already replaced all their coal plants with reactors.
However, the technology faces serious problems that have slowed its expansion.
Its main problem, in fact, is the risk of a serious accident.
Uranium, the fuel it uses, is mined mainly in a handful of countries.
Supporters argue, moreover, that it provides a steady supply regardless of the weather.
s.a: İlk cümle artı: nükleer santraller karbondioksit salmıyor. Boşluktan sonra atık ve artan maliyet, yani eksiler sıralanıyor; artıdan eksiye geçiş zıtlık ister. "However" ile ciddi sorunları tanıtan genel cümle oturuyor. "moreover" ile yeni bir artı ekleyen şık ardından gelen eksilere köprü kurmuyor.

s.q: Volunteering is often seen as something people do purely to help others. ---- Studies have found that people who volunteer regularly tend to report higher levels of happiness and lower levels of stress. Some research even suggests that volunteering may be linked to better physical health in older adults.
o: As a result, many charities depend almost entirely on volunteers.
For this reason, most volunteers expect nothing in return.
Older adults, for example, often have more free time than younger people.
Yet there is growing evidence that it benefits the volunteers themselves as well.
Volunteering, however, can be stressful when the work is emotionally demanding.
s.a: İlk cümle yaygın görüşü veriyor: gönüllülük yalnız başkalarına yardımdır. Boşluktan sonra gönüllülerin daha mutlu olduğunu gösteren çalışmalar geliyor; geçiş zıtlık ister. "Yet" ile gönüllüye de yarar sağladığını söyleyen şık köprüyü kuruyor. Stres yarattığını söyleyen şık sonraki "lower levels of stress" ile çelişiyor.

s.q: For most of history, the majority of people could neither read nor write. ---- In the Ottoman Empire, for example, the first Turkish printing house did not open until 1727, nearly three centuries after Gutenberg. As schools spread in the nineteenth century, literacy rose rapidly, transforming politics, work and family life.
o: The invention of printing, however, quickly made books available to everyone.
Most ancient texts, as a result, survived only because they were copied by hand.
Today, more than four out of five adults in the world can read.
Newspapers, for example, became cheap enough for workers to buy in the 1830s.
Literacy spread slowly, and at very different speeds in different parts of the world.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "for example" ile bir ülkede matbaanın çok geç açılması anlatılıyor; boşluk örneklenen genel cümle olmalı. Okuryazarlığın yavaş ve bölgeden bölgeye farklı hızda yayıldığını söyleyen şık bu gecikmeyi kapsıyor. Matbaanın kitapları hemen herkese ulaştırdığını söyleyen şık örnekteki gecikmeyle çelişiyor.

s.q: The idea that we use only ten per cent of our brains is one of the most persistent myths in popular psychology. Brain-imaging studies show that even simple tasks activate many different regions, and over the course of a day virtually every part of the brain is used. ---- If large parts of the brain were truly unused, damage to them would have no noticeable effect. In reality, injury to almost any area produces some kind of impairment.
o: Some people still believe that they could become geniuses if only they learnt to use more of their brains.
The brain accounts for only about two per cent of the body's weight but uses a fifth of its energy.
Psychology became a popular subject among university students in many countries during the twentieth century.
Brain-imaging techniques have become much cheaper and more widely available over the past twenty years.
Evidence from patients with brain injuries points to the same conclusion.
s.a: Paragraf, beynin yalnız yüzde onunu kullandığımız efsanesine karşı kanıt sıralıyor: önce görüntüleme çalışmaları. Boşluktan sonra hemen her bölgedeki hasarın bir bozukluk yarattığı anlatılıyor; boşluk bu ikinci kanıta geçiş. Beyin hasarlı hastalardan gelen kanıtın "the same conclusion"a vardığını söyleyen şık oturuyor.

s.q: Many cities around the world have introduced bicycle-sharing schemes in recent years. ---- Users can pick up a bicycle at one station and leave it at another, paying only for the time they use it. Supporters say the schemes reduce traffic and pollution. They also encourage people to take more exercise.
o: However, many people still prefer to ride their own bicycles.
Cycling in heavy traffic, however, can be dangerous where there are no separate lanes.
As a result, traffic in most city centres has already fallen sharply.
These schemes allow people to hire a bicycle for short journeys around the city.
These schemes are often paid for by advertising companies in return for space on the bicycles.
s.a: İlk cümleden konu bisiklet paylaşım sistemleri. Boşluktan sonra "Users can pick up a bicycle…" ile sistemin nasıl işlediği anlatılıyor; öncesinde sistem tanıtılmalı. Kısa yolculuklar için bisiklet kiralamayı anlatan şık oturuyor. Reklamla finansmanı anlatan şık da "These schemes" diyor ama kullanıcılara bağlanmıyor.

s.q: The International Space Station orbits the Earth at a height of about four hundred kilometres. ---- As a result, the astronauts on board see a sunrise or a sunset roughly every forty-five minutes. This unusual rhythm makes it difficult for them to maintain a normal pattern of sleep.
o: It was built by five space agencies working together over more than a decade at enormous cost.
Astronauts must exercise for about two hours a day to prevent their muscles from weakening.
At this altitude, it travels so fast that it completes an orbit in about ninety minutes.
The station can sometimes be seen from the ground as a bright moving point of light.
Supplies are delivered to the station by unmanned spacecraft several times a year.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "As a result" var: boşluk, her kırk beş dakikada bir gün doğumunun sebebi olmalı. "At this altitude" ile ilk cümledeki yüksekliğe bağlanan, istasyonun bir turu yaklaşık doksan dakikada tamamladığını söyleyen şık sebebi veriyor. Yapım maliyeti ve egzersiz bu sonuca bağlanmıyor.

s.q: Rubbish dumped in the oceans does not stay where it is thrown. ---- Over time, floating debris accumulates in these areas, forming vast patches of plastic. The best known of these, in the North Pacific, contains millions of small fragments that are extremely difficult to remove. Because plastic breaks down very slowly, these patches are likely to remain for decades even if no more waste enters the sea.
o: Most of it, in fact, sinks to the sea floor within a few days.
As a result, beaches near large cities are usually the most polluted.
This is mainly because most plastic is lighter than water.
Some of it is eaten by seabirds and turtles, which mistake it for food.
Ocean currents carry it across great distances and gather it in large rotating systems known as gyres.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "these areas" var; referansın karşılığı boşlukta bir bölge olmalı. Akıntıların çöpü taşıyıp "gyres" denen girdaplarda topladığını söyleyen şık hem ilk cümleyi sürdürüyor hem bölgeyi veriyor. Çöpün dibe battığını söyleyen şık sonraki "floating debris" ile çelişiyor; öteki şıklarda bölge yok.

s.q: Handwriting is taught less and less in schools as students increasingly use keyboards. ---- Some studies have found that students who take notes by hand remember lecture content better than those who type. One possible reason is that writing by hand is slower, which forces students to summarise and process information rather than copy it word for word.
o: Typing is a skill that most young people learn without any formal teaching.
Many famous writers wrote their novels entirely by hand.
This trend worries some researchers, who believe that writing by hand helps learning.
The layout of modern keyboards was first designed for typewriters in the nineteenth century.
Some schools have banned mobile phones from classrooms altogether.
s.a: İlk cümle okullarda el yazısının azaldığını söylüyor; boşluktan sonra elle not alanların daha iyi hatırladığını gösteren çalışmalar geliyor. "This trend" ile ilk cümleye bağlanıp araştırmacıların kaygısını ve el yazısının öğrenmeye katkısını veren şık iki tarafı birleştiriyor. Klavye tarihi ve telefon yasağı limit dışı.

s.q: Minimum wage laws set the lowest amount that employers are allowed to pay their workers. ---- Opponents, on the other hand, argue that forcing employers to pay more leads them to hire fewer people, especially the young and the unskilled. Economists have studied the question for decades without reaching a clear agreement.
o: In many countries, it is therefore adjusted every year to keep pace with inflation.
Some economists, for example, believe it should be abolished altogether.
The level at which it is set, moreover, varies widely from one country to another.
Supporters claim that such laws protect workers from exploitation and reduce poverty.
Wages, however, vary considerably from one industry to another.
s.a: İlk cümle asgari ücret yasasını tanımlıyor. Boşluktan sonra "Opponents, on the other hand" var: boşlukta karşı tarafın, yani destekçilerin görüşü olmalı. "Supporters claim that such laws protect workers…" bu karşıtlığı kuruyor. Ücretin ülkeden ülkeye değiştiğini ekleyen şık bir taraf sunmuyor.

s.q: Public opinion polls have become an essential part of modern politics. ---- The classic example is the 1936 American presidential election, when a magazine that had polled more than two million readers predicted the wrong winner, because its readers were wealthier than the average voter. Modern polling companies therefore devote enormous effort to selecting samples that represent the whole population.
o: Their accuracy, however, depends less on how many people are asked than on who is asked.
The first opinion poll was conducted by a local newspaper in Pennsylvania during the election of 1824.
Most polls today are carried out by telephone or over the internet.
Politicians often commission private polls before announcing a new policy.
Election results are usually announced within a few hours of the polls closing.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "The classic example" ile iki milyon kişiye sorup yanlış tahmin yapan anket geliyor. Boşluk örneklenen genel cümle: doğruluğun kaç kişiye değil kime sorulduğuna bağlı olduğunu söyleyen şık hem örneği hem "therefore" ile gelen örneklem çabasını kapsıyor. İlk anketin tarihi limit dışı.

s.q: Every year, millions of tourists visit Venice. ---- Many local people complain that the crowds make daily life difficult and push up the cost of housing. In response, the city has introduced an entry fee for day visitors on its busiest days.
o: As a result, the city's economy depends almost entirely on visitors.
Most of them come in summer, when the city is at its most beautiful.
The city has therefore decided to build new hotels outside the historic centre.
Venice is built on more than a hundred small islands linked by bridges.
Although tourism brings money to the city, it also causes serious problems.
s.a: İlk cümle artı: her yıl milyonlarca turist geliyor. Boşluktan sonra yerel halkın şikâyetleri ve "In response" ile alınan önlem, yani eksi geliyor. Artıdan eksiye geçişi "Although … it also causes serious problems" kuruyor. Ekonominin turizme bağlı olduğunu söyleyen şık yorumu artıda bırakıyor, şikâyetlere köprü kurmuyor.

s.q: Economists have long noted that people often make decisions that do not serve their long-term interests. ---- One explanation is that the immediate costs of such behaviour, such as giving up a pleasure today, feel much larger than benefits that will only appear in the distant future. Policies that make the desired choice the default option, such as enrolling employees automatically in pension schemes, have proved effective in addressing this tendency.
o: Pension schemes were first introduced in Germany in the nineteenth century.
Economics became a separate academic subject only in the late nineteenth century.
Some economists argue that governments should never interfere in personal decisions.
Employees often change jobs several times during their careers.
Many save too little for retirement, for example, even when they know they should save more.
s.a: Boşluktan sonra "such behaviour" var; boşlukta uzun vadeli çıkara hizmet etmeyen bir davranış örneği olmalı. Emeklilik için çok az biriktirmeyi "for example" ile veren şık referansı karşılıyor ve sondaki emeklilik planı önlemine de bağlanıyor. Planların tarihi ve devlet müdahalesi limit dışı.

s.q: The Library of Alexandria is often imagined as having been destroyed in a single, dramatic fire. ---- Ancient sources describe several episodes of damage over a period of centuries, and the institution probably declined gradually as funding and political support were withdrawn. The popular image of a sudden catastrophe may say more about our love of dramatic stories than about what actually happened.
o: Fires, after all, were a common danger in ancient cities built largely of wood.
As a result, scholars stopped travelling to Alexandria to study.
Libraries in the ancient world were usually attached to temples or palaces.
The fire, according to this view, destroyed hundreds of thousands of scrolls in a single night.
Historians, however, believe the reality was far more complex.
s.a: İlk cümle yaygın imgeyi veriyor: kütüphane tek bir büyük yangında yok oldu. Boşluktan sonra yüzyıllara yayılan hasar anlatılıyor; arada zıtlık olmalı. "Historians, however, believe…" bu geçişi kuruyor. Yangının tek gecede eserleri yok ettiğini söyleyen şık imgeyi sürdürüp sonraki cümleyle çelişiyor.

s.q: According to the passage, Tok Pisin first developed ----.
o: as the mother tongue of children growing up in the towns of Papua New Guinea
among labourers of varied backgrounds working on plantations abroad
when German officials required a single language for colonial affairs
as a written language used mainly by churches and the local press
from a mixture of Malay and German spoken by travelling traders
s.a: Köken sorusunda ikinci cümleye gidiyoruz: Samoa ve Queensland plantasyonlarında çalışan, ortak dili olmayan işçiler. Doğru şık bunu yurt dışındaki plantasyonlarda farklı kökenden işçiler diye veriyor. Çocukların ana dili olduğunu söyleyen şık, 20. yüzyıl ortasındaki sonraki aşamayı başlangıç gibi sunuyor; zaman kayması.

s.q: It is understood from the passage that the grammar of Tok Pisin ----.
o: was taken almost entirely from English
has stayed unchanged since the nineteenth century
is simpler today than when the language first emerged
differs clearly from that of the main source of its words
was designed by linguists so that it could be used in Parliament
s.a: Dil bilgisi cümlesi 'however' ile açılıyor: sözcükler çoğunlukla İngilizceden, ama dil bilgisi 'differs markedly from English'. Doğru şık bu zıtlığı sözcüklerin ana kaynağından belirgin biçimde ayrılma diye kuruyor. Bugün daha yalın olduğunu söyleyen şık, kreolleşmede dil bilgisinin gelişkinleştiği bilgisine ters.

s.q: It can be inferred from the passage that marriages between people from different language groups ----.
o: have helped Tok Pisin to become the first language of some children
were encouraged by the government in order to spread Tok Pisin
have caused many of the country's 800 languages to disappear
were common among plantation workers in Samoa and Queensland
prevent the children of such couples from learning English at school
s.a: Kentlerde farklı dil gruplarından ebeveynlerin evlendiği yerlerde çocukların Tok Pisin'i ilk dil olarak edindiği söyleniyor. Ortak dili olmayan anne babanın evde bu dili kullanması, karma evliliklerin bu dönüşüme katkı yaptığını düşündürüyor. Yerel dillerin yok olduğunu söyleyen şık metinde bulunmayan bir sonuç.

s.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
o: To argue that English should replace the local languages of Papua New Guinea
To compare the vocabulary of Tok Pisin with that of German
To trace how one contact language arose and became a mother tongue
To criticise the way plantation workers were recruited in the past
To explain why most creoles are studied only through historical records
s.a: Parça tek bir dili baştan sona izliyor: plantasyonda pidgin olarak doğuyor, ortak dil olarak yayılıyor, sonunda çocukların ana dili oluyor. Amaç bu gelişimi göstermek. Tarihsel kayıtları anan şık yalnız son cümleye dayanıyor; sözcük karşılaştırması ise metinde olmayan bir iş.

s.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage about the 1999 studies?
o: The participants estimated how they compared with their peers.
The low scorers greatly overrated their relative standing.
The high scorers placed themselves somewhat too low.
The tests were later repeated in other countries.
Some participants received instruction in logical reasoning.
s.a: Şıkları tek tek metne bağlıyoruz: akranlarla karşılaştırma üçüncü, alt çeyreğin yüzde 12'ye karşı yüzde 60 tahmini dördüncü, eğitim altıncı, en iyilerin kendini biraz düşük koyması sekizinci cümlede. Testlerin başka ülkelerde yinelendiğine dair hiçbir bilgi yok; cevap o şık.

s.q: According to the passage, Kruger and Dunning believed that poor performers misjudged their results because ----.
o: they did not take the tests seriously
the skills they lacked were also needed to spot mistakes
their peers had given them misleading information about the tests
the tests of humour were unfairly designed
they had received too much training beforehand
s.a: Beşinci cümle açıklamayı veriyor: doğru cevaplamak için gereken bilgi, doğru cevabı tanımak için gereken bilgiyle aynı. Eksik beceri hatayı görmeyi de engelliyor. Eğitim şıkkı sırayı ters çeviriyor; eğitim sonradan verildi ve değerlendirmeyi düzeltti.

s.q: It can be inferred from the passage that the training session ----.
o: made the top performers more confident in their own abilities than before
had no effect on how participants judged themselves
supported the researchers' explanation of the low scorers' errors
was given only to students who scored highest on grammar
showed that self-evaluation cannot be changed by teaching
s.a: Eğitim, açıklamayı sınamak için verildi; ardından düşük puanlılar kendilerini daha isabetli değerlendirdi. Beceri artınca hatayı görme de arttığına göre açıklama desteklenmiş oluyor. Etkisiz kaldığını ya da öğretimle değişmeyeceğini söyleyen şıklar yedinci cümleye ters.

s.q: One can understand from the passage that the highest scorers underestimated their relative position because they ----.
o: expected others to have done about as well as they had
believed the tests had been designed to trick them
made more errors than they had realised
were less interested in the tasks than the students who scored lowest
had received no training in logical reasoning
s.a: Gerekçe sekizinci cümlenin sonunda: "apparently assuming that others had found the tasks as easy as they had". Başkalarının da kendileri kadar iyi yaptığını sanmak bunun yeniden ifadesi. Fark edilmeyen hatalar düşük puanlılara ait; grup kayması. Puanlarını zaten isabetle değerlendirmişlerdi.

s.q: According to the passage, the main idea behind taxes on sugary drinks is that ----.
o: making such drinks more costly should discourage people from buying them
the money raised should be spent on treating diet-related diseases
poorer families will benefit more than richer ones from lower sugar intake
people should be made more aware of the link between sugar and obesity
the cost should fall most heavily on people with low incomes
s.a: Verginin çıkış fikri "The idea is simple" cümlesinde: içecek pahalanırsa daha az alınır. Doğru şık: "making such drinks more costly should discourage people from buying them". Yoksul ailelerin daha çok yararlanacağı, vergiyi savunanların eleştiriye cevabı; temel fikir değil.

s.q: It is stated in the passage that the tax introduced in the United Kingdom ----.
o: was the first tax of its kind anywhere in the world
led to a sharp fall in purchases among poorer families
was introduced at the same time as the tax in Mexico
was based on how much sugar each drink contained
was rejected by most of the companies that make soft drinks
s.a: Birleşik Krallık'ın yolu 2018 cümlesinde: üreticiler "according to the amount of sugar in their drinks" vergilendirildi. Doğru şık: "based on how much sugar each drink contained". Yoksul hanelerde alımın düştüğünü söyleyen şıkta konu tutuyor ama limit tutmuyor; o bilgi Meksika'ya ait.

s.q: It can be inferred from the passage that supporters and critics of sugar taxes disagree mainly about ----.
o: whether high sugar consumption is actually linked to obesity and type 2 diabetes
how much sugar the drinks sold in Mexico contained before 2014
which country was the first to introduce a tax on sugary drinks
how quickly soft drink companies are able to reduce the amount of sugar in their drinks
whether the effects of the taxes on people with low incomes are fair
s.a: Çıkarım sorusu; son iki cümleyi karşılaştırıyoruz: eleştirenlere göre vergi en çok düşük gelirliye yük ("fall most heavily"), destekleyenlere göre en çok onlar yararlanır ("stand to benefit most"). Ayrılık, etkinin düşük gelirliler için adil olup olmadığında. Şeker-obezite bağı tartışılmıyor; parça onu olgu olarak veriyor.

s.q: According to the passage, before the Atlantic cable was laid, ----.
o: telegraph messages between Europe and North America took several weeks
news could travel across the ocean only as quickly as a ship could sail
Queen Victoria and President Buchanan regularly exchanged messages
Cyrus Field had already laid several cables beneath other oceans
most news from Europe reached America by way of Ireland and Canada
s.a: Kablodan önceki durum ilk cümlede: haber Atlantik'i "no faster than the ships that carried it" geçiyordu ≈ only as quickly as a ship could sail. Telgrafın haftalar sürdüğünü söyleyen şık metinde yok; kablodan önce okyanusu aşan bir telgraf hattı bulunmuyordu.

s.q: It is understood from the passage that the cable completed in the summer of 1858 ----.
o: was laid by the Great Eastern on its first voyage across the Atlantic
linked Valentia with Heart's Content and remained in use for many years
made a famous exchange of greetings possible but soon ceased to function
was paid for entirely by the British government after earlier failures
broke during the operation before a single message could be sent along it
s.a: 1858 yazındaki hat Kraliçe Victoria'nın selamını iletmeyi sağladı, "but it failed within a few weeks". failed within a few weeks ≈ soon ceased to function. Valentia–Heart's Content hattı 1866'ya ait; zaman kaymış.

s.q: The Great Eastern is mentioned in the passage as a ship that ----.
o: succeeded in laying a working cable on its very first attempt in 1865
carried Cyrus Field to London so that he could meet new investors
was damaged during the lavish celebrations held in New York in 1858
was used only to recover sections of cable lost in earlier attempts
was big enough to carry the whole length of the cable in one load
s.a: Gemiyi anan yedinci cümle: "massive enough to carry the entire cable as a single payload". entire cable ≈ the whole length, single payload ≈ one load. İlk denemede başardığını söyleyen şık aynı cümleye ters: hat yolun üçte ikisinde koptu.

s.q: It can be inferred from the passage that Cyrus Field ----.
o: was not discouraged by a series of technical and financial setbacks
abandoned the project entirely after the failure of the 1858 cable
relied on government money rather than on private investors
personally designed the instruments that were used on the cable
considered the 1866 cable less important than the one laid in 1858
s.a: Çıkarım altıncı cümleye dayanıyor: kopan kablolar ve ağır kayıplara karşın Field 'nevertheless persisted' ve yeni para topladı. persisted ≈ was not discouraged, kopan kablo + kayıp ≈ technical and financial setbacks. 1858'den sonra projeyi bıraktığını söyleyen şık nevertheless'i görmüyor.

s.q: According to the passage, the direction of a bee's straight run during the waggle dance ----.
o: shows how many worker bees should leave the hive to collect the food
shows the position of the food relative to the sun
changes according to the amount of food the bee has found at the source
shows how far the food is from the hive
remains exactly the same wherever the food happens to be located
s.a: Koşunun yönü metinde aynen tanımlanıyor: "tells them where the food is in relation to the sun". Doğru şık: "shows the position of the food relative to the sun". Uzaklığı gösterdiğini söyleyen şık iki bilgiyi karıştırıyor; uzaklığı yön değil koşunun uzunluğu veriyor.

s.q: It is stated in the passage that the length of the waggle run ----.
o: gives information about the distance between the hive and the food
was not properly understood until long after Karl von Frisch had died
tells the other bees which type of flower they should visit
becomes gradually shorter as the dancer grows tired
is the only part of the dance that the other bees pay attention to
s.a: "the longer the waggle, the greater the distance": koşu uzadıkça mesafe artıyor. Bu, "gives information about the distance between the hive and the food" demek. Diğer arıların yalnız bu kısma baktığını söyleyen şık keskin ifade ("the only") taşıyor ve metinde karşılığı yok.

s.q: It can be understood from the passage that bees following the dance ----.
o: learn the direction of the food mainly from the sounds the dancer makes
can usually reach the richest flowers before the dancer returns to them
may still have to search once they reach the general area of the food
can work out the distance to the food from the direction of the straight run
find food more slowly than bees that search on their own
s.a: Doğru şıkkın yerini "Later studies" cümlesinde buluyoruz: dans "not perfectly precise", bu yüzden izleyen arılar varınca yine de arama yapıyor. Doğru şık: "may still have to search once they reach the general area of the food". Uzaklığı koşunun yönünden çıkardıklarını söyleyen şık karıştırıyor; uzaklığı koşunun uzunluğu veriyor.

s.q: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
o: why honeybees prefer flowers that grow close to their hive
the scientific career of an Austrian researcher and the Nobel Prize he received in 1973
the ways in which bees defend their colony against danger
how honeybees use a special movement to tell one another where food can be found
the reasons why some bees fail to find enough food in winter
s.a: Ana fikir sorusu; konu sallanma dansı, limit yiyeceğin yönünü ve uzaklığını bildirmesi. Parça baştan sona bunu anlatıyor: "how honeybees use a special movement to tell one another where food can be found". Avusturyalı bilim insanının kariyeri ve ödülü tek cümlelik bir detay; aşırı dar.

s.q: According to the passage, the complex sugars in human milk ----.
o: are digested by the infant's own enzymes before they reach the colon
feed certain gut bacteria instead of nourishing the infant directly
protect the baby from bacteria that come from the hospital
are turned into butyrate by the cells lining the infant's colon
make the gut community resemble that of an adult within months
s.a: Şekerleri anlatan cümlede iki ipucu var: bebek onları "cannot digest" ve kalın bağırsakta belirli bakterilere besin oluyorlar. Doğru şık bunu bebeği değil bakterileri beslemek diye veriyor. Bebeğin kendi enzimleriyle sindirildiğini söyleyen şık metnin tersini kuruyor.

s.q: It is understood from the passage that the way a baby is delivered ----.
o: determines the make-up of its microbiome for the rest of its life
matters less than the age at which breastfeeding comes to an end
affects how quickly the infant is able to digest human milk
decides whether the child will later need courses of antibiotics
influences which microbes first settle in its intestine
s.a: Doğum şeklini karşılaştıran cümlede normal doğumla ve sezaryenle doğan bebeklere "initially" ve "at first" farklı mikroplar yerleşiyor. Doğru şık bu ilk yerleşimi söylüyor. Mikrobiyomu ömür boyu belirlediğini söyleyen şık zaman sınırını atıyor; topluluk sonradan beslenmeyle değişiyor.

s.q: It can be inferred from the passage that the gut microbiome of a six-month-old baby who is fed only on milk ----.
o: is probably less varied than that of an adult
is identical to the bacteria of the mother's birth canal
contains no species of Bifidobacterium at all
can already break down every kind of dietary fibre
has been shaped entirely by the method of delivery
s.a: Katı gıda çeşitliliği "rapid" biçimde artırıyor ve topluluk ancak üç yaş civarında yetişkininkine benziyor. Henüz yalnız süt alan bir bebeğin topluluğu bu yüzden büyük olasılıkla daha az çeşitli; probably kesinliği de doğru ayarlıyor. Bifidobacterium içermediğini söyleyen şık ters: süt tam da bu bakterileri besliyor.

s.q: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
o: the risks of giving antibiotics to very young children
the differences between vaginal and caesarean births
how the gut microbiome forms and what it does for the body
the nutritional value of human milk for growing infants
the reasons why some gut microbes cause serious diseases in adults
